Read distro options where the SDK reads them

Address the fourth Copilot review on #84: options inside the distro call's
parentheses but outside the SDK's own options no longer count.

- Node.js: only the `a365` options object counts: inline, by variable,
  shorthand, or a spread one level deep. `instrumentationOptions:
  { custom: { useS2SEndpoint: true } }` does not.
- .NET: only `.Agent365` (or `.Agent365.Exporter`) assignments count, so
  `workloadOptions.UseS2SEndpoint = true` inside the callback does not.
- Python: only the call's own keyword arguments count (plus `**` spreads), not
  keywords of a nested call. The call itself is masked when initializers are
  looked up, because Python keyword arguments look like assignments.
- When the options cannot be read statically (a method group, a factory call,
  or a callback that never touches Agent365), the whole file is checked
  instead, to avoid false positives.

description:
Export observability over S2S with app-only tokens in every auth mode

Telemetry now always uses the Observability API S2S route (/observabilityService/)
with an app-only token for the exporting agent identity. Registered blueprint agent
instances therefore need no Agent365.Observability.OtelWrite permission or admin
consent; OBO / Agentic User tokens are used only for workload (MCP / Graph) calls.

- instrument-observability references: app-only token resolver scaffolds for
  Node.js, Python and .NET that reuse the hosting connection (FMI assertion for the
  turn's agent identity, then agent-identity client_credentials); S2S route flag in
  every auth mode; migration path for existing delegated wiring; .NET options moved
  to the flattened Microsoft.OpenTelemetry 1.0.3+ API (o.Agent365.*).
- Stop hooks and a365-code-validator: require the S2S route flag and flag delegated
  telemetry tokens (new findings, hook/standalone parity tests).
- Provisioning, test-local, shared detection, docs and evals: registration-based
  authorization; AI Teammates keep the OtelWrite application-role step.

Related: microsoft/Agent365-nodejs#290, microsoft/Agent365-Samples#339,
microsoft/Agent365-devTools#501

description:
fix(functions): avoid recreating a deleted task queue on functions:delete (#10685)

* fix(functions): avoid recreating a deleted task queue on functions:delete

functions:delete failed for onTaskDispatched functions whose Cloud Tasks
queue had already been deleted out of band. disableTaskQueue calls
updateQueue, which issues a queues.patch (create-or-update), so patching
the missing queue tried to recreate it and failed with "The queue cannot
be created because a queue with this name existed too recently".

Guard the update with a getQueue existence check, mirroring upsertQueue:
skip the patch when the queue is already gone (404) and rethrow otherwise.

* fix(functions): type the caught error in disableQueue and assert the rethrown error

Address review: drop the `any` escape hatch in the getQueue catch block in
favor of an inline type for the response error, and make the non-404 test
assert that disableQueue rethrows the exact upstream error instead of
accepting any rejection.

description:
fix: v2 to v1 downgrade failing with CPU error (#10889)

* fix: v2 to v1 downgrade failing with CPU error

* fix: narrow the platform-change guard to cpu and fail fast on downgrade

Memory and timeout are valid on both generations, and the platform-equality
guard also skipped them for gcfv2 vs run, which is a legal update. Gate only
cpu, and reject a gcfv2-to-gcfv1 downgrade in validation so the error appears
before the source is uploaded rather than in the release plan.

* fix: also reject redeploying a Cloud Run service as gcfv1

Skipping cpu inheritance for gcfv1 removed the only thing that stopped a
deploy from trying to update an existing `run` endpoint into a gcfv1
function, which then failed with an opaque API error mid-deploy. Share one
predicate between validation and the release planner so the two checks
cannot drift, and cover both platforms.

* test: pin the downgrade check ahead of the timeout check

inferDetailsFromExisting copies timeoutSeconds regardless of platform, so a
downgraded endpoint reaches endpointsAreValid carrying a timeout that is legal
on gcfv2 and not on gcfv1. Nothing failed if the downgrade check moved below
validateTimeoutConfig, which would report the 540s limit instead of the real
reason.

* fix: tell the user how to recreate a function as GCFv1

The downgrade error said what was not allowed but not what to do about it.
Users hitting this usually want the downgrade, so name the delete command.

* test: cover the Cloud Run to GCFv1 downgrade and the delete instruction

* chore: add changelog entry for the GCFv1 downgrade error

* fix: report every downgraded function, not just the first

noGenerationDowngrades threw on the first offender, so downgrading a
whole codebase to gcfv1 meant one error and one redeploy per function.
Collect the messages and throw once, matching validateTimeoutConfig.

* fix: reject the v2 to v1 downgrade before inheriting existing settings

Move the downgrade check into prepare's phase 2.5, ahead of source prep and
inferDetailsFromExisting. Nothing is inherited from the existing function by
then, so the cpu passthrough guard is no longer needed and is reverted.

Also drops stale CHANGELOG entries picked up from merged release resets, and
moves the Cloud Run coverage off the release planner onto
generationDowngradeMessage, since there are no run platform node functions yet.

description:
Minor Changes

  • #15928 7f57b1c Thanks @ichernetsky-cf! - Allow "us" as a jurisdiction for Container applications

    Container placement constraints now accept constraints.jurisdiction: "us" in Wrangler and typed Cloudflare configuration. This makes the US jurisdiction available alongside "eu" and "fedramp".

Patch Changes

  • #15974 7f700ef Thanks @martinezjandrew! - Fix wrangler containers list to report live instances

    The LIVE INSTANCES column now reports each application's active runtime instances instead of its configured instance count, matching the Cloudflare dashboard. JSON output continues to expose the configured count through the existing instances field.

  • #15980 90e6a1b Thanks @martinezjandrew! - Accept Durable Object application IDs in Containers commands

    wrangler containers instances and wrangler containers delete now accept the 32-character hexadecimal application IDs returned for Durable Object-backed applications, in addition to legacy dashed UUIDs.

  • #15871 6a4b0fe Thanks @tw4! - Retry transient API failures in wrangler workflows instances list and wrangler workflows instances describe

    Previously, a single temporary 5xx response or dropped connection made these read-only commands exit with an error, even though the next request would have succeeded. They now use Wrangler's existing bounded API retry handling. The read that resolves --id latest is retried too, which also benefits the other wrangler workflows instances commands that accept latest; the mutating requests they make afterwards are not retried. Persistent failures are still reported after the retries are exhausted, and under --json any retry notices are written to stderr so stdout stays valid JSON.

  • Updated dependencies []:

    • miniflare@5.20261001.0-alpha

chore(build): publish mongosh to Ubuntu 26.04 9.0 PPA MONGOSH-3701 (#2856)

* chore(build): publish mongosh to Ubuntu 26.04 9.0 PPA MONGOSH-3701

Reverts a8cf01fd (MONGOSH-3582). Ubuntu 26.04 was deferred out of 9.0.0
because the server was blocked on SERVER-131155; that is now fixed and
SERVER-131625 confirms 26.04 ships in 9.0.0. Re-add ubuntu2604 to the
9.0.0 PPA list so mongosh is published to the resolute 9.0 repos.

* chore(ci): pin Ubuntu 20.04 e2e variants to 8.3.x, run linux-n24 on 22.04

MongoDB 9.0 does not support Ubuntu 20.04, so 'stable' (now 9.0.2) has
no download for those hosts. Pin the 20.04 e2e variants to 8.3.x, the
newest server with 20.04 builds, keeping their OpenSSL 1.1 coverage.
Run the Linux unit-tests-only variant on Ubuntu 22.04, which resolves
the latest server by default.

* chore(ci): pin PPC e2e variants to 8.3.x

Server-side JS tests (mapReduce, $function) and the currentOp tests
fail consistently on ppc64le against server 9.0.2, while passing on
x64/arm64 against 9.0.2 and on ppc64le against 8.3.x. Pin the PPC
variants to 8.3.x and drop the RHEL 9 PPC 8.3.x variant it duplicates.

* chore(build): cover deb-arm64 in barque tests, list Ubuntu 26.04 target

Add a deb-arm64 case to barque.spec.ts so the published arm64 URLs,
including resolute 9.0, are asserted alongside deb-x64.

Add ubuntu2604 to the deb server-like target list so the Download
Center lists Ubuntu 26.04 for the deb packages. The server publishes
9.0.2 ubuntu2604 builds to cloud.json but not yet to full.json, so

v11.1.4


Security


Fixes a path-traversal escape (bypass of GHSA-mp2f-45pm-3cg9)
where a chain of symlink entries lets an archive write/read files
outside the output directory, potentially leading to RCE.


Affected: <= 11.1.3


    

  • Resolve link/directory targets with realpath before the
containment check
    • 

  • Re-validate created symlinks resolve inside the output dir (catches
self-referential chains)
    • 

  • Refuse hardlinks that target a symlink
    • 

  • Write files with O_NOFOLLOW
    • 

  • Reject duplicate entry paths
    • 



Advisory: GHSA-hrh2-vp3x-79xf


Full changelog: https://github.com/XhmikosR/decompress/compare/v11.1.3...v11.1.4


v11.1.3


Security


Fixes a crafted archive being able to read or write files outside the
extraction directory:


    

  • Validate symlink and hardlink targets against the output
directory
    • 

  • Replace the prefix-based containment check with
path.relative, fixing a sibling-directory bypass
    • 

  • Strip setuid, setgid, and sticky bits from extracted files
    • 



Advisory: GHSA-mp2f-45pm-3cg9
(CVE-2026-53486)


Other changes


    

  • Write regular files before hardlinks so a hardlink to an extracted
file resolves
    • 

  • Internal refactoring of the extraction code

description:
feat: simplify copy in deploy progress (#8541)

Deploy progress described its steps in terms that felt more like
implementation details rather than something the user would care about
("Finished hashing", "CDN requesting 0 files, 0 functions, and 0 edge
functions").

Also, the messages never mentioned the Netlify Server, even though it
was already being hashed and uploaded.

The messages now name the server alongside files and functions, say what
is happening rather than how, and stay quiet when there is nothing to
upload.

Along the way this fixes `buildStatsString` returning an empty string
for a single item, which is why a static-only deploy printed a bare
"Finished hashing", plus a long-standing "1 functions" plural and a
"nothing to deploy" guard that only counted files and functions.

Before, on a deploy with no changes:

```
Finished hashing 3 files and 1 functions
CDN requesting 0 files, 0 functions, and 0 edge functions
Uploading 0 files
Finished uploading 0 assets
```

After:

```
Deploying 3 files, 1 function and a server
Everything is already uploaded
```

Supabase CLI v2.119.0 — 2026-09-30

This release delivers stability improvements for local development with 30+ fixes focused on Docker container management, networking, and connection handling. Key fixes address Docker Desktop compatibility on macOS and Windows, session persistence, and request routing. OrioleDB configuration graduates from experimental to stable.

Highlights

  • Storage uploads fixed on Docker Desktop for macOS — Resumable uploads and S3 endpoints now work through the gateway. (#6921)
  • Stack connection details visible on start — Database URL, MCP endpoint, and other connection info show immediately after launch for easier debugging. (#6894)
  • OrioleDB configuration is now stable — Move from experimental_oriole to standard oriole config. (#6828)

New features

  • Type generation languages from registry — gen types automatically picks up new language targets as Supabase adds them. (#6822)
  • Studio MCP server at /mcp — Serve Studio's Model Context Protocol server for AI agent and third-party tool integration. (#6898)
  • Edge function testing improvements — New testing entrypoint and Promise-based API. (#6841)

Improvements

  • Docker preferred over Podman for automatic runtime selection. (#6859)
  • Containers named by project and service for visibility. (#6867, #6870)
  • Studio stays active 5 minutes after last request. (#6866)
  • Function deno.json files loaded as Deno configuration. (#6907)

Bug fixes

  • Storage and network connectivity on Docker Desktop (macOS and Windows). (#6921, #6887)
  • Stacks clean up when Docker is unavailable. (#6825)
  • Migra session settings persist through database reconnects. (#6884)
  • Local functions read request bodies before responding. (#6830)
  • Escape sequences in quoted strings no longer split incorrectly. (#6906)
  • Yes/no prompts reject unrecognized answers. (#6910)
  • Database socket connections require authentication. (#6833)
  • Postgres containers stop cleanly. (#6834)
  • Upstream connections reused across proxied requests. (#6925)
  • Image pulls retry on transient registry failures. (#6879)
  • Mailpit database isolated per stack. (#6901)
  • SMS provider configuration handled when unset. (#6685)

Plus internal improvements and dependency updates.

fix(cli): accept the short stack id from stack list in --stack-id (#6967)

## Summary

**TL;DR:** `supabase stack list` prints an 8-character stack ID, but
every `--stack-id` flag rejected it and required the full 64-character
id. Every stack command now accepts the short ID from the list, or any
unique prefix of at least four characters, the same convention git and
docker use. The list table keeps its compact column.

### Before

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  L["stack list"] --> S["ID column: 8 chars"]
  S --> D["stack destroy --stack-id abcd1234"]
  D --> E["error: must be a lowercase SHA-256 stack id"]
```

### After

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["--stack-id value"] --> B{"4-64 lowercase hex?"}
  B -->|no| E["flags error + hint"]
  B -->|64 chars| F["exact lookup"]
  B -->|4-63 chars| D["match saved stacks by prefix"]
  D -->|none| N["not found: run stack list"]
  D -->|several| G["ambiguous: lists full ids"]
  D -->|one unreadable| I["read error surfaced"]
  D -->|one| OK["full id used"]
  F --> OK
```

### Why

Copying the ID column from `stack list` into `stack destroy --stack-id`
(or `stop`, `status`, ...) failed with `--stack-id must be a lowercase
SHA-256 stack id`, so users had to rerun the list with `--output-format
json` to find the real id.

### What changed

- The shared stack target resolver accepts a full id (unchanged exact
lookup) or a unique lowercase-hex prefix of 4 or more characters. This
covers `destroy`, `stop`, `start`, `restart`, `status`, `logs`, and
`prepare`.
- A prefix matching several stacks fails with a flags error listing
every matching full id. A prefix matching a stack whose saved state is
unreadable surfaces the read error instead of reporting it missing.
- "Not found" and malformed-id errors now point to `supabase stack
list`.
- The `status --env` pointer printed by `stack start` repeats the
resolved full id rather than the typed prefix.
- Flag help, command `SIDE_EFFECTS.md` files, and
`docs/stack-commands.md` describe prefix selection.

- The stack package's `discover` takes an `idPrefix`, so a prefix lookup
only probes the owners of matching stacks. A full id keeps the direct
lookup.

### Terminal captures

Recorded with `vhs` from source on the base commit and on this branch,
against two native demo stacks (`default`, `feature-a`) in a throwaway
`SUPABASE_HOME`. Each capture runs `stack list`, destroys `feature-a`
with the 8-character ID from the list, then lists again.

**Before:** the listed ID is rejected and both stacks remain.


![before-destroy-short-id](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/avallete/e9becd6013177475950a54a532b2bff3/raw/before-destroy-short-id.gif)

**After:** the listed ID resolves to the full id, `feature-a` is
destroyed, and `default` remains.


![after-destroy-short-id](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/avallete/e9becd6013177475950a54a532b2bff3/raw/after-destroy-short-id.gif)

## Linked issue

Closes
[CLI-2609](https://linear.app/supabase/issue/CLI-2609/stack-text-stack-list-shows-an-8-character-id-that-stack-id-rejects)

fixes `stop --no-backup` leaving the

diff` or `db pull`

since the native `db diff` and `db pull` port in v2.108.0, `docker run

description:
fix(stack): reserve native backend ports below the ephemeral range (#6941)

On the native runtime, a reopened stack intermittently failed to start
Logflare with `port 46477 already in use` / `eaddrinuse`. This showed up
in the native "eager lifecycle and reopen" stack E2E on Linux CI.

`ProcessRecipe` reserved each native backend port by binding port 0 and
releasing it before spawning the service. That port comes from the OS
ephemeral range (Linux: 32768–60999). In the gap, an unrelated outgoing
connection can take it as its source port and leave it in TIME_WAIT, and
the service's own bind then fails.

Backend ports are now reserved by `Ports.ts`, with the same
below-ephemeral scan that public auto allocation uses (ADR 0017):
- Ports claimed by any saved stack are skipped, so a backend can't take
a sticky public port that another stack will reclaim on its next start.
Backend ports are never saved as claims.
- Occupancy uses the same `accepts`-based check as public ports. A
loopback-only probe bind can coexist with a wildcard listener on macOS,
BSD and Windows, which hid ports already published by Docker.
- When an attempt loses its bind to another listener, that port is
excluded from the retry, so retries try a different port.

The window between releasing the probe and the child binding, and the
retry count, are unchanged.

description:
fix(cli): name the changed setting and the fix when a saved stack rejects a config change (#6944)

When `supabase start` (with `[experimental] stack`) refuses a change to
a saved stack, the error now says which setting changed and what to do
about it. It used to report internal paths such as `endpoints.http` with
a generic suggestion.

- Each rejected change is reported as the `config.toml` key, or the
`SUPABASE_*` environment variable that set it, with the saved and
requested values, after a lead-in saying the saved stack cannot adopt
them. For example: `[db] major_version: saved 17, requested 15`, or
`[api] port: saved automatic, requested 54999`.
- Changes across all affected services are reported together in one
error. A shared `[api] port` appears once.
- The suggestion offers two ways out: revert the setting to keep the
stack and its data, or run `supabase stack destroy --stack-id ` to
recreate it. It warns that recreating deletes the local database data.
The ID is used so the command targets this stack regardless of the
current directory. When a change can't be reverted, such as a
catalog-pinned artifact or Postgres build from a CLI upgrade, the
suggestion offers only the destroy command.
- JSON and stream-json errors carry the same details in structured form
(`stack_changes` with service, path, key, saved and requested values,
plus `recreate_command`), so agents don't have to parse prose.
`stack_changes` keeps one entry per affected service, and
`recreate_command` omits `--yes`, which a JSON-mode destroy requires.

Port settings are now defined once in `stack-config.ts`, shared by
config translation and error attribution, so a new port can't be added
to one and missed in the other. The tests use the real composition
planner.

description:
ci(stack): retry slim pickup when a merge-queued PR holds the branch (#6957)

`slim-release-published.yml` force-pushes one branch per service release
line. When that branch's PR sits in the merge queue, GitHub rejects the
push (GH006) and the job used to fail, dropping the planned pin until
the next upstream release. On 2026-10-01 this lost edge-runtime
v1.77.4-r0: the v1.77.3-r0 and v1.77.4-r0 dispatches both hit
`slim-bump/edge-runtime` while #6930 was queued (restored by #6955).

When a push is rejected because the branch is queued for merging, the
Apply step now:

- waits for the queue to merge or drop that PR, polling `isInMergeQueue`
for up to 30 minutes and within the app token's lifetime;
- stops processing the current plan, so no remaining item is built from
the pre-merge base;
- re-sends the same dispatch so a fresh run re-plans from the updated
default branch, at most three times in a row (tracked by a validated
`client_payload.replay` counter).

The concurrency group now keeps every pending run (`queue: max`) instead
of replacing the pending one, so a replay can never cancel a newer
dispatch and its release-visibility wait. A failed queue lookup or
dispatch, a queue that holds the branch past the deadline, an exhausted
replay budget, and any other push rejection still fail the run with the
manual recovery command. ADR 0026 documents the behavior.

description:
fix(cli): cache the upgrade check outside projects and for --version (#6939)

## Summary

**TL;DR:** The upgrade notice no longer calls the GitHub releases API on
every run outside a project or on every `supabase --version`. Outside a
project the latest tag is now cached in `/cli-latest` for
ten hours, and root `--version` uses the cache like every other command.
The notice text, the `SUPABASE_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER` opt-out, and
project-dotenv precedence are unchanged.

### Before

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Command succeeds"] --> B{"real supabase/ dir?"}
  B -- yes --> C{"--version?"}
  C -- no --> D{"cache fresh?"}
  D -- yes --> E["read supabase/.temp/cli-latest"]
  D -- no --> F["fetch GitHub, write cache"]
  C -- yes --> F
  B -- no --> G["fetch GitHub every run, no cache"]
```

### After

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Command succeeds"] --> B{"real supabase/ dir?"}
  B -- yes --> C["supabase/.temp/cli-latest"]
  B -- no --> D["SUPABASE_HOME/cli-latest"]
  C --> E{"fresh and no symlink?"}
  D --> E
  E -- yes --> F["read cached tag"]
  E -- no --> G["fetch GitHub, write tag or empty backoff"]
```

### Why

The cache lived only in `supabase/.temp/cli-latest` and was written only
when `supabase/` existed, so any command run outside a project fetched
`api.github.com/repos/supabase/cli/releases/latest` before exiting. Root
`--version` always bypassed the cache. Each fetch blocked exit for up to
a 3s timeout on slow or offline networks, and unauthenticated calls
count against GitHub's 60 requests per hour per IP; repeated runs
exhaust that quota quickly.

### Performance

Median wall time over alternating `develop` / PR launches on one
machine, each build with its own `SUPABASE_HOME` (10–15 runs per row,
5–6 for the hung-network and first-run rows, one warmup). "Hung network"
is a local proxy that accepts the connection and never answers. Outside
a project, `develop` never caches, so it calls GitHub on every run; this
PR reads `/cli-latest` after the first run.

**Improved:** runs where `develop` calls GitHub and this PR reads a
cache or backs off.

| Scenario | `develop` | This PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outside a project, `--version` | 209 ms | 133 ms | −37% |
| Outside a project, `completion zsh` | 221 ms | 142 ms | −36% |
| Inside a project, `--version` | 206 ms | 130 ms | −37% |
| Outside a project, hung network, `--version` | 3174 ms | 154 ms | −95%
|
| Outside a project, hung network, `completion zsh` | 3168 ms | 159 ms |
−95% |
| First run, hung network, `--version` | 3367 ms | 1107 ms | −67% (800ms
timeout) |

**Controls (expected unchanged):** both builds do the same work.

| Scenario | `develop` | This PR | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| First run with an empty cache, `--version` | 241 ms | 245 ms | both
fetch once |
| Inside a project, `completion zsh` | 137 ms | 140 ms | both read the
project cache |

#### Trace

Median `UpgradeNotice.check` span duration from `SUPABASE_TRACE_FILE`
traces of alternating launches (10 runs, 5 for the first run). `develop`
has no child fetch span, so its check duration is its GitHub request.

| Scenario | `develop` check | This PR check | This PR
`UpgradeNotice.fetch` | This PR attributes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Improved: outside a project, `completion zsh` | 79.9 ms | 0.6 ms |
none (0/10) | `cache.location=user`, `cache.hit=true` |
| Improved: inside a project, `--version` | 76.3 ms | 0.5 ms | none
(0/10) | `cache.location=project`, `cache.hit=true` |
| Control: first run with an empty cache, `--version` | 77.4 ms | 78.4
ms | 77.1 ms (5/5) | `cache.location=user`, `cache.hit=false` |
| Control: inside a project, `completion zsh` | 1.1 ms | 1.7 ms | none
(0/10) | `cache.location=project`, `cache.hit=true` |

### What changed

- A real `/supabase/` directory keeps using
`supabase/.temp/cli-latest` exactly as before.
- Otherwise the tag is cached in `/cli-latest`
(`SUPABASE_HOME` from the shell env, default `~/.supabase`), with the
same ten-hour TTL and empty-file offline backoff.
- The symlink protections apply to the new location: a symlinked
`SUPABASE_HOME` (including spellings with a trailing `/` or `/.`) or
cache file disables the cache, and the write still uses `O_NOFOLLOW`.
- Root `--version` no longer forces a fetch, so a release published
within the last ten hours may surface on a later run instead of
immediately.
- The release fetch times out after 800ms instead of 3s. A round trip to
`api.github.com` normally takes well under that; a slower fetch falls
through to the empty-file backoff, so on such networks the notice is
skipped until the next check.
- The `UpgradeNotice.check` span records `cache.location` (`project`,
`user`, or `disabled`) and `cache.hit`, and a cache miss runs the GitHub
request as an `UpgradeNotice.fetch` child span, so traces and `bench-cli
--trace` show when the check pays for a network round trip.
- `resolveSupabaseHome` accepts any `{ join }` implementation so the
hook can reuse it with `node:path`.
- The new state file is documented in `apps/cli/docs/supabase-home.md`.

test(stack): ignore the host-gateway probe when listing whole-stack workloads (#6952)

The Docker whole-stack E2E "eager lifecycle and reopen" failed
intermittently on its identity check
(`identity.endsWith(databaseMarker)` in
`tests/whole-stack/scenarios.ts`).

`tests/whole-stack/workloads.ts` listed Docker workloads by the
`com.supabase.stack` label alone. The container runtime's host-gateway
probe (`readProbeHosts` in `Container.ts`) is a short-lived `docker run
--rm` container that carries the stack labels but deliberately no
`com.supabase.instance` label, since it isn't an instance. When the
listing ran while the probe was still exiting, the probe's bare
container ID was taken as a workload identity. Running the probe command
in a loop while polling the same `docker ps` filter catches it
mid-flight on most iterations.

The listing now only counts containers carrying `com.supabase.instance`
or `com.supabase.stack-managed=true`, which are the labels that identify
stack workloads. The probe still removes itself, so the check that every
workload is gone at stop keeps its coverage. Product code is unchanged.

description:
fix(stack): wait for native processes to exit before reporting them stopped (#6937)

When a native service ignores its graceful stop signal past
`gracefulStopTimeout`, `NativeProcess.killProcess` fell back to
SIGKILLing the launcher and its process group. It returned without
confirming that either had exited, so `stop` could report a service
stopped while its workload still held its port or files, and a
replacement started right after could collide with it.

On macOS and Linux the fallback now kills the workload's process group
first, while the launcher is still alive to reap its direct child, then
waits for the launcher to exit. If the launcher hasn't exited within the
graceful-stop timeout, it is force-killed and its exit is awaited, so
stop always settles. Windows behaviour is unchanged.

The tests drive the timeout with `TestClock`. They prove `kill` stays
pending until the launcher's exit is confirmed, and that a launcher that
never reaps is force-killed.

Waiting on deeper detached descendants of the workload would need a
launcher protocol change and is out of scope.

description:
fix(stack): write instance root owner markers atomically (#6933)

`InstanceRoot.integration.test.ts` › "lets concurrent first claims of a
fresh root all succeed" failed intermittently.

`ensureOwnedInstanceRoot` claimed a fresh root by writing the owner
marker with `writeFile(…, { flag: "wx" })`. Node implements that as an
exclusive `open` followed by a separate `write`. In that window a
concurrent claimer could see the marker file already created but still
empty, compare it against its own marker, and fail with "belongs to
another instance".

The marker is now written in full to a unique temporary file beside the
root and hard-linked into place. `link` is atomic and fails with
`EEXIST` when the marker already exists, so it keeps the exclusivity of
the old exclusive create without ever exposing a partial file. Every
claimer then validates the marker that landed: concurrent claims for the
same instance succeed, and conflicting claims still fail. The temporary
file is always removed.

A new integration test covers conflicting concurrent first claims, where
exactly one may win.

description:
fix(cli): stop typegen stdin feed hanging on an early-exit tool (#6948)

`types.typegen-host.integration.test.ts` › "survives a tool that exits
before reading a large stdin" intermittently hit its 5s timeout when the
machine was busy.

The typegen host writes the request to the tool's stdin and waits for
that write to finish. When the write hits backpressure, it waits for a
`drain` that never comes once the reader has exited. The only way out is
the pipe's `error` (EPIPE) event. Under load, that event can be
delivered before the listener for it is attached, so the feed hangs even
though the tool's exit code, stdout and stderr have all resolved.

The stdin feed is now raced against the child's exit, which is always
observable once the tool is gone, so the wait no longer depends on
winning that scheduling race. Under the same CPU load, the test failed 2
times in 50 before the change and 0 times in 50 after.

The stack's `CommandRunner` stdin path already races its feed against
process exit, and it stays settled when several MB of stdin are fed to a
psql that exits immediately.

description:
docs(repo): add a test-audit skill with an authoring gate and an audit mode (#6890)

## Problem

Nothing limits test growth, and agents write a test for nearly every
change. The rules against low-value tests live as prose in the "Test
quality" section of `AGENTS.md`, which agents skim past when they add or
review tests.

## Change

- Adds `.agents/skills/test-audit/SKILL.md`, which loads whenever a test
is written, changed or reviewed. It includes:
- **Authoring gate:** four questions a new test must answer before it's
added.
- **Level rule:** one primary test per contract, at the strongest
boundary that can reach it.
- **Junk-pattern checklist:** fitted to our Effect layers, handler
integration tests and `runSupabase()` e2e, including real-time waits on
production timeouts.
  - **Retention bar and regression-test rule.**
- **Read-only audit mode:** a retain / fix / consolidate / delete ledger
with one evidence line per mark.
- "Test quality" in `AGENTS.md` points to the skill and drops the
redundant-coverage bullet, which the skill now covers.
- `.claude/skills/` holds one symlink per repo skill (`effect`,
`test-audit`) into `.agents/skills/`, so Claude Code discovers them
automatically and Codex keeps reading `.agents/skills`. `.gitignore` now
ignores `.claude/*` except `.claude/skills`, and local state such as
worktrees and settings stays ignored. A new skill in `.agents/skills`
needs a matching symlink.

description:
feat(cli): trace CLI runs end-to-end with opt-in OTLP export (#6935)

## Summary

**TL;DR:** Every CLI run can now produce one OpenTelemetry trace that
shows where time goes, down to individual migrations, containers, health
waits, API operations, and SQL statements. Export is opt-in per run
(`SUPABASE_TRACE_FILE` for a local OTLP/JSON file, or
`SUPABASE_OTLP_ENDPOINT` for Tempo/Jaeger/Grafana), costs nothing when
unset, and never exports free-form text or secrets. Two new scripts turn
traces into answers: `trace-report` (critical path, self time, repeated
spans) and `bench-cli` (fair A/B timing between two binaries, optionally
per span).

### Before

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["CLI run"] --> B["ad-hoc spans
(uneven coverage)"]
  B --> C{"telemetry consent?"}
  C -->|yes| D["~/.supabase/traces/*.ndjson
no parent ids, never read"]
  C -->|no| E["dropped"]
  B -->|--debug| F["one stderr line per span"]
```

### After

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["CLI run"] --> R{"SUPABASE_TRACE_FILE
or SUPABASE_OTLP_ENDPOINT?"}
  R -->|neither| N["tracer disabled
no-op spans, no I/O"]
  R -->|set| T["cli.run span tree
commands, phases, I/O, processes"]
  T --> S["sanitizer
no free text, no secrets"]
  S --> F["OTLP/JSON file"] --> TR["trace-report / bench-cli"]
  S --> O["OTLP collector
Tempo, Jaeger, Grafana"]
```

### Why

Benchmarking or debugging the CLI meant adding temporary instrumentation
for each investigation. The existing tracer wrote consent-gated NDJSON
without parent span ids, so no span tree could be rebuilt, and nothing
read those files. Agents and maintainers need one consistent trace per
run that standard tools can open.

### What changed

- **Export pipeline** (`apps/cli/src/shared/telemetry/`): one sink per
run (file xor OTLP/HTTP, both is a config error); CLI-namespaced
variables so a global `OTEL_*` setup never receives CLI internals;
`TRACEPARENT` is adopted as the parent and passed to child processes;
the trace scope flushes within a bounded window before
`processControl.exit`.
- **Tracing off by default**: without a sink the root runs with
`TracerEnabled = false` and the exporter module is never loaded. Startup
and command wall time match `develop` within noise.
- **Sanitizer**: exported batches keep only structured data — exception
events keep `exception.type` (plus a structured SQLSTATE), status and
log messages are dropped, SQL text becomes `db.operation.name` and a
per-run salted hash, URLs lose query strings and storage object keys,
headers are allowlisted, resource attributes are allowlisted, trace
files are `0600`.
- **Instrumentation sweep** across commands, `command-internal`,
`shared`, `packages/stack`, and `packages/api`, following the new
conventions ADR: named spans at I/O and service boundaries, handler
phase spans, outcome annotations (counts, cache hit/miss, attempts, exit
codes), process spans with the docker verb, API spans named by operation
id, no spans per poll attempt or loop item.
- **`SUPABASE_DEBUG=1` console** keeps its behavior (spans up to depth 2
plus failures on stderr) with sanitized, length-capped attributes;
`--debug` alone still prints no spans.
- **Scripts**: `apps/cli/scripts/trace-report.ts` and
`apps/cli/scripts/bench-cli.ts` (alternating launches, isolated
environment, warm-up, untimed traced/profiled launches, `--cpu-prof`).
- **Removed** the NDJSON sink and the dead `command-instrumentation.ts`
copy of the command span.
- **Docs**: [ADR 0027](docs/adr/0027-cli-tracing-conventions.md) for
conventions and
[tracing-monitoring.md](apps/cli/docs/tracing-monitoring.md) for usage;
telemetry docs updated for the removed NDJSON files (old
`~/.supabase/traces` files are no longer written and are safe to
delete).

### Terminal captures

Recorded from a fresh corpus project against a local `grafana/otel-lgtm`
and with `vhs`; both builds are local binaries of `develop` and this
branch.

**Tempo: CLI runs, `supabase start` waterfall, cold `db diff` breakdown,
a sanitized process span, two commands grouped by `TRACEPARENT`**

per-span bench**

test(repo): remove test Docker volumes once per run by creation label (#6923)

Docker-backed stack tests left a named `supabase-db-*` volume behind on
every run.

Docker database storage keeps one shared volume per state root and
daemon. Stack destroy deliberately clears only the stack's namespace
inside it, because the volume is shared with other stacks and holds the
snapshot cache. Tests that run a Docker database under a temporary state
root destroyed the stack and then deleted the root. After that, nothing
could find the volume again.

This PR cleans up those volumes in one place per test run instead of in
each test:

- When `SUPABASE_STACK_TEST_RUN` is set, `DockerDatabaseStorage` adds a
`com.supabase.stack-test-run=` label to the volumes it creates, and
the container runtime adds it to the containers it creates. Nothing else
changes, and nothing changes when the variable is unset.
- `packages/stack/tests/docker-volume-run.ts` is a vitest `globalSetup`
for the stack and CLI integration and E2E projects. It generates a
random id unless an outer invocation already owns one. Its teardown
removes exactly the stack-managed volumes carrying that id, without
force, and fails the run if a removal fails. It skips when Docker is
unavailable.
- Vitest workers, CLI subprocesses and detached stack owners inherit the
id. `processEnvLayer` keeps it when it replaces the environment.
- Docker test state roots must stay private to a run. The
`Commands.integration` Docker variants passed a bare temporary directory
as the database root, which made them share one never-removed volume
keyed to the parent of `$TMPDIR`. They now use `makeDockerDatabaseRoot`
like the other database service tests.
- The stack-cache E2E's own marker-based volume cleanup is removed.

- Under Bun, vitest exits on SIGINT and SIGTERM without running
globalSetup teardown, so an interrupted run used to leave its volumes
behind and its containers running. The owning setup now records a
per-user, host-local marker with its pid, and deletes it at teardown.
Each new run's setup finds markers whose process is dead and removes
that run's labelled containers, then its labelled volumes, then the
marker. Live runs, other machines sharing the daemon, and unlabelled
resources are never touched.

Volumes created before this change carry no run label and are not
cleaned up automatically.

## Summary

A shallow-module audit of `apps/cli` found two kinds of cleanup. Each
candidate was checked with the deletion test: remove the module and
paste its body into every caller. If the callers end up no longer, the
module was only passing work through.

**Dead code.** Knip did not flag these because each file's only importer
was its own colocated unit test.

crypto, credentials, platform-api, token, errors). Live replacements are
`src/auth/command-*.ts` and `src/command-internal/login-*.layer.ts`.

plus the two matching die-placeholders in `run.ts` and the mock in
`tests/helpers/mocks.ts`.
- `shared/output/table.ts` and `shared/output/time.ts`.

exports `dbConnectionLayer` directly.
- `OutputFormatFlag` moves into `command-internal/global-flags.ts` with
the other globals.
- The region display table is hoisted once to
`command-internal/region.format.ts` and shared by backups and projects.

instead of through per-command aliases; its coverage moves to the

- `tracing.service.ts`, `db-bootstrap/messages.ts`,
`standalone-analytics-config.layer.ts`, `supabaseHome()`,

- `packages/cli-test-helpers` exports `harness.ts` directly instead of

(`src/shared/telemetry/__fixtures__/error-tags.txt`) drops the four tags
that belonged to the deleted modules: `ApiError`,
`InvalidLocalServiceVersionsStateError`, `InvalidTokenError`, and

`apps/cli/README.md` architecture list now points at `src/auth/` and

No behaviour change. Span names and telemetry command paths are

description:
feat(cli): tag command telemetry with stack backend and OrioleDB (#6940)

## Summary

**TL;DR:** `cli_command_executed` now records which local backend a
command ran on (`stack_backend`: `legacy` or `stack`), which runtime its
stack uses (`stack_runtime`: `docker`, `podman`, or `native`), and
whether the project selects an OrioleDB image (`orioledb`). With these,
error rates can be compared per command between the legacy and new stack
backends (and per container or native runtime), and between OrioleDB and
standard Postgres projects, before the new stack becomes the default.

### Before

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["supabase <command>"] --> B["resolve backend
(legacy for unrouted)"]
  B --> C["handler runs"]
  C --> D["cli_command_executed
no backend, no engine"]
```

### After

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["supabase <command>"] --> B{"routed by
experimental.stack?"}
  B -->|yes| C["StackBackendContext
legacy or stack"]
  B -->|no| D["no backend"]
  C --> E["handler runs"]
  D --> E
  E --> F["config read records
orioledb true/false"]
  E --> R["stack lookup records
stack_runtime"]
  F --> G["cli_command_executed
+ stack_backend
+ orioledb
+ stack_runtime"]
  R --> G
```

## Why

Command telemetry had no way to tell whether a command ran on the new
stack runtime or the legacy one, so we couldn't measure the new
runtime's adoption or failure rate. It also couldn't separate OrioleDB
projects from standard Postgres ones.

## What changed

- `resolveStackBackend` returns no backend for commands that
`experimental.stack` does not route (and for `--version`). The root
command provides `StackBackendContext` only when a backend was selected.
Handlers still default to legacy, so routing behavior is unchanged.
- `withCommandTelemetry` adds `stack_backend` when a backend was
selected. It also provides a command-scoped attribute sink, so code
below the handler can add properties to the command event.
- `orioledb` is recorded wherever local database config is resolved: the
legacy config reader, Postgres image resolution, and stack config
loading. The stack records it before rejecting OrioleDB, so failed stack
starts on OrioleDB projects are attributed. The value describes local
config only; it doesn't describe remote targets such as `--linked` or
`--db-url`.
- `stack_runtime` is recorded where a stack-backend command learns its
stack's runtime: runtime selection for new and shadow stacks, the
project stack lookup used by local database commands, and the stack
target resolver used by `stack` commands. Commands without a single
stack (stack-mode `services`, `stack stop --all`) omit it.
- Removed the unused shared `withCommandInstrumentation` wrapper and the
unused `flags_used`/`flag_values` context fields. `docs/analytics.md`
now describes the current wrapper, event shape, flag redaction and base
properties.

## Linked issue

Closes CLI-2589
Closes CLI-2590

Merge pull request #27 from DefiLlama/perp-funding-rates

replace yields/perps with api/perpFundingRates
replace yields/perps with api/perpFundingRates

Release notes

359 merged pull requests since 2.0.0, from 29 contributors.

Upgrade every Sepolia node to 2.1.0 before the Glamsterdam fork on Tue, 06 Oct 2026, 13:53:36 UTC.

For most nodes this is an in-place upgrade with no resync. Read Breaking changes first if you run on the flat backend with a custom sync config, run poacore, run a Flashbots relay, parse Parity-style traces, or build plugins against Nethermind. **

Highlights

  • Glamsterdam on Sepolia. Final EIP-8037 state-gas rules, the TX_MAX_TOTAL_GAS_LIMIT transaction cap, and Engine API alignment for Amsterdam. (#13140, #13484, #13627, #13554, #13583, #13586, #13755)
  • Faster EVM. The interpreter loop is replaced by tail-call chain dispatch, stack words stay in UInt256 limb layout, storage values stay as UInt256 until they are persisted, and JUMPDEST analysis is rewritten. (#13128, #13323, #13420, #13189, #13810)
  • Lower engine_newPayload latency. The response goes out as soon as the block has executed and its roots match, before the commit. engine_forkchoiceUpdated still waits for that head's commit. GC pauses no longer stall payloads the way they did. (#13647, #13711, #13476, #13334)
  • Per-transaction changeset index for flat archives (opt-in). A single-transaction trace starts at its target transaction instead of replaying the whole block before it: debug_traceTransaction went from ~7.1 s to ~28 ms in the PR's measurements. Whole-block traces run their transactions in parallel (6–10× faster). Enable with FlatDb.HistoryTransactionIndexEnabled=true. (#13454, #13426)
  • BAL healing after snap sync (flat backend). On the flat backend, the state left by snap sync is healed by replaying block access lists instead of downloading trie nodes. It is on by default (Sync.BalHealing=true); set it to false to go back to trie-node healing. snap/2 is advertised only when BAL healing can run. (#12945)
  • Dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 networking. RLPx, discv4 and discv5 listen on both families, ENRs advertise both, and there is a new Network.ExternalIpV6 override. (#12679, #12982, #12983, #13731)
  • Flat backend safety rails. A flat DB that RocksDB had to auto-repair is now re-synced instead of trusted. Unsafe flat activations are refused at start instead of silently corrupting or discarding state. (#13645, #13644)
  • Reclaim the patricia trie after a trie→flat conversion. FlatDb.DropPruningTrieState=true deletes the old trie store on the next start once the flat DB owns the state (~227 GB on mainnet). Off by default. (#13572)
  • RocksDB 11 through Nethermind's own bindings. The RocksDB package is replaced with Nethermind.RocksDbBindings (RocksDB v10 → v11): source-generated P/Invoke with no marshalling stubs, and every native handle held in a SafeHandle. (#12853)
  • New EF bootnodes. The EF bootnode entries for mainnet, Sepolia and Hoodi are replaced with the new NodeOps fleet: five dual-stack nodes running both discv4 and discv5. (#13313)
  • More zkVM targets. Stateless guests for SP1 and OpenVM ship alongside ZisK, and the ZisK toolchain moves to 1.3.0-alpha. (#13435, #13769, #13743)

Performance

  • EVM dispatch and call frames: 3.8–4.5% faster block processing on the superblocks, realblocks and fusaka benchmark sets. (#13189)
  • Storage values held as UInt256: SLOAD 9–18%, SSTORE 42% and TSTORE ~50% faster, with no allocations on those paths. (#13420)
  • EVM stack in limb layout: 45–53% faster ADD, 16–36% faster SUB, and 9–18% faster shifts. (#13323)
  • JUMPDEST analysis: worst-case analysis of 64 KiB initcode (a 200 MGas block of PUSH1/JUMPDEST patterns) drops from 0.4–3.2 s to 22–153 ms, depending on the SIMD tier. Initcode is analysed on first use. (#13810)
  • Trie and storage-key hashing: 35–80% less time on transaction and receipt-root workloads. (#13552)
  • Prewarming: a single fan-out while senders arrive gives superblocks processing a median −4.4%, P99 −27.9%, and +7.6% MGas/s. Prewarming and trie concurrency caps are removed, and parallel work is budgeted across the state root, blooms, the receipts root and prewarming (2–4% faster processing). (#13640, #13388, #13770)
  • Carried caches: pre-block account and storage caches are carried across blocks. (#13100)
  • Discovery traffic: on a warm-started Hoodi node, discovery traffic fell by 90% (152 KiB/s → 15 KiB/s), and the standalone bootnode uses ~44% less working set. (#13122)
  • Snap sync: downloads are bounded and overlap with response processing. Whale-storage verification in FlatTrieVerifier is parallelised. (#12623, #12615)
  • RPC: eth_call, eth_estimateGas and eth_createAccessList no longer hash the transaction on every run (~0.2 ms on large calldata) (#13804). the stream interpreter is off by default because it lost on every measured eth_call shape. eth_getFilterChanges is served from shared block logs. (#12999, #13742)
  • Intel hybrid CPUs: block processing is pinned to the performance cores by default (Blocks.ProcessingCores). Nothing changes on other CPUs. (#13717)

⚠️ Breaking changes

If you run a node (config and startup)

  • poacore / poacore_validator now ship FlatDb.Enabled=false because they use FastSync without SnapSync (#13644). A node on those configs that synced on 2.0.0 is on the flat backend, since flat is 2.0.0's default. On 2.1.0 it refuses to start (Refusing --FlatDb.Enabled=false on an existing flat DB). Either pass -FlatDb.Enabled=true, or delete the flat, flatHistory and persistedSnapshot directories and resync the state.
  • -FlatDb.Enabled=false on an existing flat DB is refused. In 2.0.0 the node silently discarded the state and resynced (#13428). It now stops with an error. (#13644)
  • Flat + Sync.FastSync=true + Sync.SnapSync=false is refused on a fresh node. Legacy tree sync on the flat backend can leave holes in the state. An already-synced node keeps running and logs a warning. The exception is importing from patricia (FlatDb.ImportFromPruningTrieState=true on a datadir that holds patricia state). (#13644)
  • New FlatDb.OnRepair setting, default Resync. If RocksDB auto-repairs the flat DB, the node now wipes the flat state and runs state sync again. Headers, bodies and receipts are kept. Archive nodes synced from genesis cannot snap-resync. Set FlatDb.OnRepair=Ignore and plan a resync yourself if a repair is ever reported. (#13645)
  • Receipt.MaxBlockDepth default raised back from 1,000 to 10,000, and the limit is now also enforced on eth_getFilterLogs. On nodes with the log index, only blocks the index cannot serve count towards the limit. A filter created by eth_newFilter over a wider range is still accepted, but eth_getFilterLogs on it fails with 32602. (#13131)
  • Removed config keys: FlatDb.EnablePreimageRecording, Db.PreimageDbRocksDbOptions, Db.PreimageDbAdditionalRocksDbOptions (#13690), LogIndex.VerifyRpcResponse (#13131), and Grpc.Enabled, Grpc.Host, Grpc.Port along with the gRPC endpoint (#13330). A JSON config that still sets them logs Invalid configuration settings at startup. Remove them from configs, environment variables and command-line flags.
  • Merge.CompactMemory default changed from Yes to No. This removes GC compaction stalls from engine_newPayload. Steady-state RSS may be somewhat higher. (#13476)
  • Init.LogRules no longer routes to Seq, and Seq.MinLevel is now the floor for the Seq target. To send a namespace's Trace output to Seq, add an explicit writeTo="seq" rule in NLog.config. (#13419)
  • Dual-stack by default. With Network.LocalIp unset, the P2P TCP and discovery UDP listeners now try to bind [::] on Linux and Windows, so the P2P port may now be reachable over IPv6. Check your firewall. macOS stays IPv4-only. Set Network.LocalIp=0.0.0.0 to keep IPv4-only. (#12982)
  • Pruning.FullPruningTrigger=VolumeFreeSpace with a threshold too low to ever trigger now logs a startup warning. Automatic pruning was already not running in that case, so nothing new is broken. (#13485)

If you run a Flashbots relay

  • Flashbots.EnableValidation now defaults to true. flashbots_validateBuilderSubmissionV3 checks the submitted block's state root, receipts root, gas used and logs bloom against its execution. Set it to false explicitly to get the old behaviour. (#13452)

If you integrate over JSON-RPC / Engine API

  • eth_getHeaderByNumber("pending") returns null, matching go-ethereum and execution-apis#877. (#13082)
  • proof_getTransactionByHash / proof_getTransactionReceipt return result: null for a transaction they cannot serve, instead of a 32000 error. proof_getTransactionReceipt returns 32002 when the block can no longer be retraced. (#13366)
  • Parity vmTrace stack pushes are hex quantities (0x0, 0x1), not byte strings. Word operations now report their pushes. (#13750, #13487)
  • Other trace output changes. Empty trace selections are accepted. trace_get keeps lookup errors instead of replacing them. trace_filter returns an error when the requested history is unavailable, and buffered trace_filter now applies a single JsonRpc.Timeout to the whole request. Deleted-account fields carry deletion markers. callTracer omits to on a failed top-level CREATE. (#13667, #13676, #13677, #13668, #13078)
  • EIP-3155 / structLogs traces are corrected: gasUsed is the top-level execution-gas delta, refunds are cumulative, and opcode names follow Geth (0x44 is reported as DIFFICULTY). (#12981)
  • eth_estimateGas runs entirely against the requested block, the way eth_call does, with a single deterministic search. Before, the first run used a synthetic next-block header. Estimates can differ from 2.0.0 within the error margin. Invalid-opcode and stack failures now return the standard error texts (for example invalid opcode: INVALID, stack underflow (0 <=> 2)), and eth_call uses the same texts. (#13899)
  • eth_call with maxPriorityFeePerGas above maxFeePerGas (after London) fails before any gas is bought, with the same max priority fee per gas higher than max fee per gas error execution returns. eth_createAccessList fills the fee cap as the priority fee plus twice the base fee when only a priority fee is given. (#13904)
  • Call requests with gasPrice and a type-specific field (accessList, blobVersionedHashes, authorizationList) but no explicit type are no longer decoded as legacy transactions. eth_call, eth_estimateGas, eth_createAccessList and eth_simulateV1 results change for those requests. (#13450)
  • eth_subscribe("logs") delivers logs for every block that becomes canonical, and removed: true logs for every block that leaves the canonical chain. A subscriber that falls more than 1,000 blocks behind (or 10,000 events for pending-transaction and peer subscriptions) is disconnected. (#13451)
  • No state for a block now returns 32002 from every method, and guard-rail rejections (32002, 32005, 4444) are no longer logged at WARN. (#13643)
  • The SSZ-REST Engine API moves from /engine/v2/... to /engine/v1/..., per execution-apis#793. The JSON-RPC engine_* surface is unchanged. (#13023)
  • engine_newPayload rejects a post-Shanghai payload with a null withdrawals list (MissingWithdrawals). (#13501)
  • /data/events accepts ?events=. A client that only needs processing statistics should pass ?events=processed. (#13334)

If you build against Nethermind (plugin / library authors)

These are source-breaking changes: rebuild your plugins against 2.1.0.

  • IBackgroundTaskScheduler.TryScheduleTask now takes a request type that implements IBackgroundTaskRequest, and the source string is gone. (#9956)
  • ISyncPeerPool.Free is removed. SyncPeerAllocation is now IDisposable, so dispose it with using. (#13094)
  • World-state scopes are opened with TryBeginScope / TryBeginScopeAtTarget, which return false for an unavailable base instead of throwing. (#13522)
  • Storage APIs take UInt256 values instead of byte arrays. SlotValue is removed. (#13420)
  • EVM extension API: the gas-policy methods are TryConsume*, the OutOfGas flag is removed, and the EvmStack constructors require a CodeInfo. (#13189)
  • ProcessingOptions.Trace is removed. Use TraceProcessingOptions.ReadOnlyReplay. (#13443)
  • Value-hash and protocol API changes in the txpool and networking code. (#13592)
  • Nullable reference types are enabled in EVM, Trie, State and 7 foundation projects. (#13099, #12155)

Consensus / protocol

  • Glamsterdam (Amsterdam-gated, Sepolia from 10-06): the EIP-8037 spill is repaid after a child frame merges, and a restored spill is burnt on a top-level halt (#13140, #13484). TX_MAX_TOTAL_GAS_LIMIT (2³² − 1) is enforced in the pool, in block validation and in eth_estimateGas (#13627). The unknown-original storage flag is kept across repeated writes (#13554). The EL no longer enforces slot ordering on engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV4 (#13583). Orphaned headers are checked for a slot number (#13586). engine_getPayloadV5 is rejected from Amsterdam on (#13755).
    EIP-7928 receipt event metadata is corrected (#13509), and AuRa keeps existing accounts in BAL preprocessing (#13047).
  • XDC: randomize-contract transactions now pay and burn gas (#13359), and sign-transaction receipts are encoded as legacy in the receipts trie. The receipts change fixes a consensus divergence on typed transactions (#13375).

Sync, database & state

  • Recovery of missing contract code. (#9417)
  • A fast-sync body could be dropped by the block cache, which left the receipts stage stuck. Fixed. Nodes already stuck on this need a bodies resync. (#13474)
  • Flat persistence keeps going when the committed state is off the canonical chain. MinReorgDepth stays reachable after folding to the finalized boundary. Flat state is retained across Engine-X reorgs. (#13591, #13550, #13402)
  • A gather whose state was just persisted is retried instead of refused (fixes an occasional 32002 No state available at the block being folded). (#13763)
  • VerifyWithTrie no longer reports a false positive when an account is deleted that the trie still holds. (#13521)
  • debug_resetHead prunes flat snapshots that are unreachable from the new head. (#13524)
  • New FlatDb.EnableCarryForwardCache (default true) to turn off the cross-head read cache. (#13752)
  • The history-walk ETA overflow no longer kills progress or discards a finished archive-proof walk (this bug is present in 2.0.0). The walk also reports the replay block of a storage range. (#13761, #13791, #13604, #13754, #13620)
  • SyncServer range-broadcast serialised. Pooled lists from trie path recovery are disposed. (#12728, #13266)
  • ElapsedMicroseconds overflow on long-running stopwatches fixed. (#13416)
  • The history pruner is created before the block processor starts. (#13285)
  • When a block wipes a contract's storage, the pre-block storage cache now invalidates only that contract. Before, it dropped the whole cache and logged an Info line each time, which on pre-Cancun history meant tens of thousands of lines an hour during a full sync from genesis. (#13850)
  • The disk-space probe is skipped when the availability check is disabled. (#13456)
  • Code from a reverted CREATE no longer reaches the code DB, and code-write counters roll back with it. (#13074, #13432, #13433)

JSON-RPC & tracing

  • Malformed JSON-RPC batch items no longer abort the rest of the batch. (#12537)
  • eth_syncing reports the beacon tip as the highest block. (#12739)
  • debug_traceTransactionByBlockAndIndex resolves block tags and hashes. (#13138)
  • eth_feeHistory reward percentiles use post-refund receipt gas. (#13563)
  • eth_sendRawTransactionSync no longer misses a receipt included in the next block. (#13736)
  • Simulation cache is reset when the real chain advances. (#13444)
  • Single-transaction traces no longer replay the transactions after the target. (#13426)
  • Discarded block traces in debug_traceTransactionInBlockByIndex are disposed. (#13324)
  • EIP-7708 finalization logs are reported to tracers, and the previous transient value shows up in TSTORE traces. (#13567, #13504)
  • Account-creation results are preserved in traced and BAL-backed execution. (#13574)
  • eth_simulateV1 child headers and payload attributes inherit the parent slot number (for Amsterdam SLOTNUM). (#13584, #13585)

Engine API & block processing

  • engine_forkchoiceUpdated waits for the head's own commit, including when blocks are queued behind it, a second copy of the head is queued, or the commit is slow. (#13711)
  • Fixed a missed drain of the block processing queue. (#13749)
  • Null required Cancun payload fields are rejected. (#13747)
  • Custody columns are applied on forkchoiceUpdatedV5. (#13109)
  • FOCIL: engine_getInclusionListV1 accepts the parent block hash. (#13097)
  • The block processor split (main-only BlockchainProcessor, separate OneTimeChainProcessor), with a follow-up fix for transaction-index replay. (#13449, #13629)
  • Blocks are processed while sender recovery finishes. (#13597)

Networking & protocol

  • A Hello whose node ID differs from the authenticated peer is rejected. (#13348)
  • Outgoing receipts are capped under the devp2p message size limit. Trie-node and receipts requests have bounded lookups. The receipt log limit is derived from the block gas ceiling. (#13595, #13596, #13288)
  • Connect workers no longer dial past MaxActivePeers. (#13302)
  • Discovery event loop shutdown is bounded. (#13617)
  • Startup external-IP resolution retries before it gives up. Persisted peers keep the endpoint that was actually dialled. (#13731)

Stability & hardening

  • A malformed EthStats ping no longer terminates the node. (#13353)
  • BN254 Add/Mul input length is checked in release builds. (#13208)
  • Keccak output sizes the sponge cannot serve are rejected. (#13187)
  • A stateless rejection no longer terminates DEBUG-enabled hosts. Execution requests are recovered correctly in stateless RPC inputs. (#13535, #13346)
  • The Docker images carry Nethermind's OCI labels (source, revision, version) instead of Ubuntu's. (#13694)

L2 & other chains

  • XDC: nine XDC-specific eth_* methods are added (block signers and finality, candidates, staking ROI, token stats) (#12950). XDPoS header fields are returned over JSON-RPC and newHeads, and AuRa's step and signature are restored on newHeads (#13055). eth_getAccountInfo returns the XDC shape (#13228). Transactions under the minimum gas price are rejected at pool admission (#13222). eth_gasPrice is floored at the pool minimum (#13633). SyncInfo QC and TC are verified independently (#13296). Unsupported eth versions are no longer advertised (#13018). State sync starts without waiting for headers back to genesis (#13609).
  • Optimism: after Jovian, payload attributes from op-node (8-byte eip1559Params plus a separate minBaseFee) are accepted. Before, every engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV3 with attributes failed with 38003, which broke block building behind op-node (#13813). Blocks Nethermind builds after Isthmus now keep the L2ToL1MessagePasser storage root as withdrawalsRoot instead of the empty-list root, which op-geth and Nethermind itself reject (#13814). OP Superchain chain registry refreshed (#13043, #13179, #13430, #13606).
  • Taiko: Taiko mainnet (Alethia) uses the 0.01 gwei Shasta base-fee floor that taiko-geth and alethia-reth enforce. Before, Nethermind rejected current Alethia blocks with Invalid baseFee (#13812). Unzen zk-gas metering for failed steps matches REVM, so canonical blocks that end a step out of gas are no longer rejected (#13824).
  • Plataberget: new archive config, -config plataberget_archive. (#13073)

CLI

  • Honor CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR in aitools commands. (#6838)
  • Added --ttl and --no-expiry flags to databricks postgres create-branch so a branch's expiration can be set without hand-writing a --json spec. --ttl accepts the REST API duration form (604800s), a Go duration (168h), or day/week units (7d, 3w); --no-expiry creates a branch that never expires. One of --ttl, --no-expiry, or a spec expiration in --json is required. (#6313)
  • databricks ssh connect serverless sessions now provide Claude Code and Codex configured with Unity Gateway out of the box. (#6885)

AI Runtime

  • Add databricks air images push (Preview) to configure Docker authentication and push container images to Databricks Artifact Registry. (#6869)
  • air run now grants the configured permissions on the MLflow experiment as well as the job. (#6870)

Bundles

  • Add libraries field to clusters. (#6831)
  • Error out when a configured workspace_id does not match the connected workspace, instead of silently using it in resource URLs emitted by bundle summary. (#6754)
  • Fix spurious recreation of Lakebase (Postgres) branches, roles, and catalogs when the referenced project is updated in place: an in-place project change (e.g. display_name) no longer forces a delete + create of resources that reference the project's or branch's name. (#6865)
  • Direct engine now detects and applies an explicitly configured integer zero (e.g. gcp_attributes.local_ssd_count: 0) added to a resource first deployed without the field. (#6867)
  • Migrate existing Terraform deployment state to the direct engine before deploying (previously done after a Terraform deploy), so the deploy runs on the direct engine. (#6749)
  • The postgres_snapshot_schedules resource (introduced in v1.16.0) is now marked Beta and is no longer available in PyDABs, matching the other postgres_* resources; configure it in YAML instead. (#6887)

Gate Python tests, lint, and docs on relevant changes while keeping
generation checks unrestricted and making change-detection failures fail
all Python jobs.

## Why

Avoid unnecessary Python CI runs and transient failures on unrelated
changes.

## Tests

YAML formatting, actionlint, and `git diff --check`.

description:
Add Kiro to `databricks aitools install` (#6908)

> Recreated from #6436 as a branch in `databricks/cli` (not a fork) so
the JFrog/OIDC-gated CI jobs (`task test`, `task test-exp-aitools`,
`validate-generated`) actually run — fork PRs can't obtain the OIDC
token. Original author's commits are preserved. Supersedes #6436.

## Summary

Adds Kiro to the agent registry so `databricks aitools install` treats
it like any other skills-only agent. Follows the same shape as Goose
(#6214), Gemini CLI (#6204) and Pi (#6199).

## Why

Kiro reads agent skills from `~/.kiro/skills` (user-level) and
`/.kiro/skills` (workspace-level), each skill a directory
containing `SKILL.md` — exactly the layout this repo already emits.
Today Kiro users have to fall back to `databricks aitools install --path
~/.kiro/skills`, which works but records no state, so `aitools update`
and `aitools uninstall` never see those skills and `aitools list`
reports every one of them as `not installed`.

## Verification

Tested on macOS with Kiro 1.0.182.

Kiro's loader (`NodeProgressiveContextSource`) rejects a skill when
frontmatter is missing, when `name` or `description` is empty, when
`name` is outside 1–64 characters, when `description` exceeds 1024, or
when `name` does not equal the directory name. Everything this repo
emits satisfies that.

With 29 stable skills installed into `~/.kiro/skills`, Kiro accepted all
29. The only rejections in that directory were two deliberately
malformed probe skills added to confirm the loader was really scanning,
plus two unrelated pre-existing skills whose frontmatter `name`
disagrees with their directory:

```
skill.frontmatter.missing   zz-probe-no-frontmatter      (deliberate probe)
skill.fields.missing        zz-probe-no-description      (deliberate probe)
skill.name.mismatch         analyze-mlflow-trace         (pre-existing, unrelated)
skill.name.mismatch         analyze-mlflow-chat-session  (pre-existing, unrelated)
```

Worth knowing for anyone testing this: Kiro resolves skills lazily when
a **chat session starts**, not when the IDE launches. Installing and
then looking at an already-open Kiro shows nothing until a new session
begins.

## Notes on the registry entry

- `SkillsSubdir` is left empty because Kiro's directory is literally
`skills`, so the default applies.
- `SupportsProjectScope: true` — Kiro's own picker text documents both
scopes.
- `Binary: "kiro"` is set, but Kiro is IDE-first so the binary is
frequently absent from `PATH`. Detection then falls back to `ConfigDir`
and reports files-only, which is the correct state for a skills-only
agent (`Plugin nil`).

## Telemetry

Also adds `AitoolsAgentTypeKiro` and the matching `agentType` case, so
Kiro installs are not logged as `TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` and
`TestAgentTypeCoversRegistry` stays green.

**The Universe half is already merged, so nothing is owed on the proto
side.** That guard's failure message notes the enum lives in
`enum.proto` (Universe) as well as `aitools_install.go` (CLI). `KIRO =
10` was added to `AitoolsAgentType.Type` and merged to master on
2026-09-01 (universe 2524420), with `Protobuf-Linter-Pr` and
`OpenAPICompatibility-Pr` both green — the latter being the machine
check that the additive enum value is backward compatible. The two
changes are order-independent: the enum addition is additive, and the
CLI only emits `"KIRO"` once this PR merges. So this is the complete
change and needs a review rather than any follow-up work.

## Tests

```
go test ./cmd/aitools/... ./libs/aitools/... ./libs/telemetry/...

ok  github.com/databricks/cli/cmd/aitools              4.159s
ok  github.com/databricks/cli/libs/aitools/agents      1.529s
ok  github.com/databricks/cli/libs/aitools/installer   2.648s
ok  github.com/databricks/cli/libs/telemetry           6.616s
ok  github.com/databricks/cli/libs/telemetry/protos    2.023s
```

Test coverage added alongside the existing Goose cases: registry paths
and project detection in `libs/aitools/agents/registry_test.go`, the
skills-only assertion in `agents_test.go`, the project-scope declaration
in `libs/aitools/installer/installer_test.go`, the agent-choices
assertion in `cmd/aitools/install_test.go`, and the project-scope update
path in `cmd/aitools/update_test.go` — which needed a `.kiro` project
skills dir in the fixture alongside the existing `.pi`, `.gemini` and
`.goose` ones.

`libs/aitools/agents/detect_test.go` is deliberately not extended: Goose
and Gemini CLI have custom config-dir resolution to cover there
(`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `GOOSE_PATH_ROOT`), while Kiro uses a plain
`~/.kiro` with no env override and `registry_test.go` already pins both
of its paths.

## Changelog

`.nextchanges/cli/aitools-kiro.md`, matching the fragment the Goose and
Gemini CLI PRs each shipped.

description:
Preserve large integers exactly in `databricks api` (#6884)

`databricks api` routed the `--json` request body and the response
through `any`, so Go's `encoding/json` turned every JSON number into a
float64 and any integer above 2^53 (a job id, pipeline id, ...) lost its
low digits — `18000000000000000123` came back as `...000`, corrupting
both the request sent and the rendered response.

- **Request:** POST/PUT/PATCH send the `--json` bytes verbatim;
GET/DELETE/HEAD decode with `UseNumber`, so the id stays exact in the
query string too (a float64 renders as `1.8e+19`).
- **Response:** captured into a `*json.RawMessage` and rendered with the
new `cmdio.RenderJSONBytes` — integers, object key order, and unescaped
characters survive, while the SDK's `Accept: application/json` header
and HTML/non-JSON error handling stay intact.

Acceptance tests round-trip `18000000000000000123` through the test
server (response, POST body, and GET query) and cover the
request/response edge cases (Accept header, `null` body,
empty/HTML/malformed responses); unit tests cover the request builder
and the renderer.

This pull request and its description were written by Isaac.

---------

Co-authored-by: Isaac 
Co-authored-by: simon <4305831+simonfaltum@users.noreply.github.com>
product_or_resource: Preserve large integers exactly in `databricks api` (#6884)

Add multi-container support in CLI yaml. Now CLI will support both
singleton tasks, as well as multi-container/image multi-node tasks.
Included an example yaml.

Top level env vars are merged into each container. Each container now
has it's own definition of:

description:
direct: map secrets value/owner in DoRead; drop RemapState (#6809)

`ResourceSecret`'s `RemapState` mapped `value`/`owner` from the API's
`effective_*` fields — needed so the persisted state matches config and
re-plans show no drift — but it also zeroed the output-only metadata
(`create_time`, `effective_value`, `metastore_id`, …), dropping those
fields from the plan's `remote_state` display.

This moves the `value`/`owner` mapping into a small in-place
`remapSecretRemote` applied in `DoRead`/`DoCreate`/`DoUpdate`, and stops
zeroing the rest: the output-only fields are already
`ignore_remote_changes`, so they cause no drift and can flow through for
visibility. `RemapState` is removed. Prep toward replacing hand-written
`RemapState` with the automatic copier (#6777).

This pull request and its description were written by Isaac.

description:
[Release] Release v1.19.0

## Release v1.19.0

### CLI

 * Honor `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in `aitools` commands. ([#6838](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6838))
 * Added `--ttl` and `--no-expiry` flags to `databricks postgres create-branch` so a branch's expiration can be set without hand-writing a `--json` spec. `--ttl` accepts the REST API duration form (`604800s`), a Go duration (`168h`), or day/week units (`7d`, `3w`); `--no-expiry` creates a branch that never expires. One of `--ttl`, `--no-expiry`, or a spec expiration in `--json` is required. ([#6313](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6313))
 * `databricks ssh connect` serverless sessions now provide Claude Code and Codex configured with Unity Gateway out of the box. ([#6885](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6885))

### AI Runtime

 * Add `databricks air images push` (Preview) to configure Docker authentication and push container images to Databricks Artifact Registry. ([#6869](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6869))
 * `air run` now grants the configured `permissions` on the MLflow experiment as well as the job. ([#6870](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6870))

### Bundles

 * Add libraries field to clusters. ([#6831](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6831))
 * Error out when a configured `workspace_id` does not match the connected workspace, instead of silently using it in resource URLs emitted by `bundle summary`. ([#6754](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6754))
 * Fix spurious recreation of Lakebase (Postgres) branches, roles, and catalogs when the referenced project is updated in place: an in-place project change (e.g. `display_name`) no longer forces a delete + create of resources that reference the project's or branch's `name`. ([#6865](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6865))
 * Direct engine now detects and applies an explicitly configured integer zero (e.g. `gcp_attributes.local_ssd_count: 0`) added to a resource first deployed without the field. ([#6867](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6867))
 * Migrate existing Terraform deployment state to the direct engine before deploying (previously done after a Terraform deploy), so the deploy runs on the direct engine. ([#6749](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6749))
 * The `postgres_snapshot_schedules` resource (introduced in [v1.16.0](https://github.com/databricks/cli/releases/tag/v1.16.0)) is now marked Beta and is no longer available in PyDABs, matching the other `postgres_*` resources; configure it in YAML instead. ([#6887](https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6887))
