description:
<pre style='white-space:pre-wrap;width:81ex'>feat(ai): add `snow ai` to launch coding agents via the Snowflake AI Gateway

* feat(ai): add `snow ai claude` to launch Claude Code via Snowflake AI Gateway

Adds a `snow ai` command group whose first command launches Claude Code with
its model traffic routed through the AI Gateway of the active connection.

The gateway base URL is derived from the connection host rather than
hardcoded, and the bearer credential is taken from the CLI's own cached
authentication, so a user who has already run `snow connection test` needs no
further setup. Telemetry env vars the gateway relies on are set for the
launched process.

The user's Claude Code settings.json is never touched: everything is passed
as environment to the child process only, so the configuration lasts exactly
as long as the launched session.

Notes on the design:

* `ai` gets a no-op callback. Without one, typer collapses a group holding a
  single subcommand into that subcommand, exposing it as `snow claude`.
* Extra arguments are forwarded to the `claude` binary. Flags that snow also
  defines must be passed after a `--` separator.
* `--dry-run` prints the resolved environment and `--show-token` prints the
  live credential plus a reproducing curl, for debugging gateway responses.
* `_plugins/ai/commands.py` is excluded from the check-print-in-code hook,
  matching the existing exclusions for sql/repl.py and spcs/common.py, since
  the debugging output above is deliberately raw and shell-copy-pasteable.

Credential derivation is currently verified only for
authenticator = oauth_authorization_code; see the TODO in commands.py for the
other authenticator types and the private connector internals it relies on.

* feat(ai): add `snow ai opencode` to launch OpenCode via Snowflake AI Gateway

Adds a second agent to the `snow ai` group. OpenCode is config-driven rather
than env-driven, so the gateway is wired up through a provider block passed
inline via OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT. Nothing is written to disk; OpenCode
merges its config sources, so the user's own opencode.json (agents, MCP
servers) is preserved.

Drives OpenCode's first-class `snowflake-cortex` provider rather than
borrowing its Anthropic one, for two reasons:

* Auth. @ai-sdk/anthropic authenticates the Anthropic way, with an x-api-key
  header and no Authorization header, which the gateway rejects with 401.
  snowflake-cortex is @ai-sdk/openai-compatible and sends
  `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, which is what the gateway expects.
* Wire quirks. snowflake-cortex carries Snowflake-specific compatibility
  shims we would otherwise have to reimplement: it rewrites max_tokens to
  max_completion_tokens, repairs `"role":""` in streamed deltas and turns a
  400 "conversation complete" into a clean stop.

Its own default baseURL points at Cortex REST, which bypasses the gateway
entirely, so options.baseURL is overridden to route back through us. The
provider's loader also refuses to configure itself without an account and, in
that state, never attaches the compat wrapper above, so the gateway host is
passed as the account label.

The derived base URL carries a /v1 suffix. The Vercel AI SDK appends only the
operation path (/chat/completions) to the given baseURL, exactly as OpenAI's
own SDK does; Anthropic's official SDK is the outlier in appending
/v1/messages, which is why `snow ai claude` passes a bare host and this
command does not. An explicit --base-url is used verbatim.

--model is pinned as small_model as well as model, because OpenCode runs a
second, smaller model for thread titles that fails independently of the main
one; pinning both means a working --model implies a working session.

* feat(ai): forward agent arguments, fix credential selection, fix agent header

Three related changes to `snow ai claude` and `snow ai opencode`.

Argument forwarding. Adds `--agent-args`, a terminator after which every token is
handed to the agent verbatim. snow and the agents share around forty flag names,
almost all from snow's global connection options (--debug, --verbose, --model,
--port, --host, --token, -v, -c), and anything reaching snow's parser risks being
claimed by snow: `snow ai opencode serve --port 3000` previously lost `--port 3000`
silently. The tail is sliced off argv before click parses, so it is never examined
and a future snow global option cannot change what the agent receives. Implemented
as a TyperCommand subclass overriding parse_args; `no_args_is_help=False` is pinned
because an all-agent invocation leaves click an empty head, and click prints help
rather than launching in that case. `--` is not supported and its failure names the
replacement.

Credential selection. The authenticator declared in the connection config now
decides the credential: a programmatic access token (token or token_file_path) or a
cached OAuth access token. Anything else is refused before launch with a message
naming both supported types. The previous fallback to the driver session token was
guaranteed to fail, because the REST layer behind the gateway answers it with an
empty-bodied 401, so password, MFA, SAML and externalbrowser connections got a
confusing gateway error instead of a clear CLI one. The resolved connection view is
read via clone().update_from_config(), since a named connection's authenticator is
absent from the bare context.

Agent identification. Every request now carries `snow-agent-name: claude` or
`snow-agent-name: opencode` so the gateway can attribute traffic per agent. Claude
takes it through ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS, OpenCode through the injected provider's
options.headers, verified on the wire in both cases. It is hardcoded, as a value the
gateway relies on is only useful if it is dependable.

Also removes `--traces-exporter`, `--custom-header` and our `--model`: the agents
have native flags for all three, and `--agent-args` makes them reachable. Neither
command now defines options of its own. The OpenCode model default moves to
openai-gpt-5.4, still pinned as small_model so an overridden main model cannot break
thread titles, and a warning before launch states that Claude models return 503
through the gateway rather than leaving the default to hide it.

Because typer.echo is gone in favour of cli_console, _plugins/ai/commands.py no
longer needs its check-print-in-code exclusion.

* feat(ai): add --gateway-url to override the derived gateway address

The base URL is derived from the connection host plus a hardcoded gateway name,
which does not hold everywhere: the name has already changed once during
development, and accounts can expose the gateway at a different address.

Takes a version-less base URL. The two client SDKs disagree on where the API
version belongs - Anthropic's appends /v1/messages to what it is given, while
the Vercel AI SDK appends only /chat/completions and so needs /v1 in the base
URL - so each command re-applies its own convention and a single value works for
both. A trailing /v1 is stripped first, meaning a URL copied from the OpenCode
form cannot produce /v1/v1 and the Claude form still works for OpenCode.

The credential is deliberately left alone: it always comes from the connection's
configured authenticator, so overriding the URL cannot be used to aim a
Snowflake credential at an unrelated host without also holding a connection that
yields one.

Also restores the ability to point an agent at a local server, which is how the
header and session-propagation behaviour is verified now that there is no
dry-run output to inspect.

* docs(ai): add a short spec README to the ai plugin directory

Covers what the two commands implement, how the credential is selected, and the
design constraints that are easy to break on a later change: the SDK disagreement
over where the API version belongs, why OpenCode drives snowflake-cortex rather
than anthropic, why no_args_is_help is pinned off, and why small_model is pinned.

Links README-AI-GATEWAY.md, which nothing referenced previously.

* docs(ai): move README-AI-GATEWAY.md into the ai plugin directory

The file was added by this branch rather than inherited, and a top-level README
describing one plugin does not belong at the repo root. Moving it next to the code
also removes an orphan: nothing referenced it from the root.

Fixes three things the move exposed. It described itself as a fork of
snowflakedb/snowflake-cli, its setup steps cloned a personal fork rather than this
repo, and its link to README.md now resolves to the plugin's own spec, which is
where a reader should go next.

* feat(ai): support only PAT connections, dropping the OAuth path

Narrows credential resolution to programmatic access tokens, so this plugin reads
nothing but documented CLI connection parameters.

The OAuth path was the only thing here reaching into the CLI's own credential
handling. Because the connector clears the OAuth access token off the auth object
after login (reset_secrets), obtaining one meant reading private connector
attributes - auth_class._idp_host and _token_cache, plus TokenCache, TokenKey and
TokenType - which nothing else in src/snowflake/cli does. Those are unversioned,
a connector upgrade could break them silently, and the symptom would be a 401
rather than a clear error. Auth primitives are not this plugin's to reimplement.

A PAT has none of that: it is a documented connection parameter (token,
token_file_path), already a bearer credential, and read through the public
ConnectionContext. Removing OAuth also drops the last import from cli._app, so
the plugin is now self-contained.

OAuth would also have shipped a refresh problem. Access tokens live roughly ten
minutes, the credential is captured once at launch, and neither agent re-reads it,
so a session outlives its credential with nothing positioned to notice - the 401
occurs between the agent and the gateway, where the CLI is not in the path. A PAT
sidesteps this entirely.

The OAuth work is preserved on at-ai-gateway-cli-oauth for a separate change.
Connections using any other authenticator are refused before launch with a message
pointing at a PAT.

* docs(ai): document model identifiers and live-verification requirements

The README named neither the default model nor the shape a model identifier
has to take, which is the first thing anyone hits. Both are now recorded,
along with the constraint behind them: the gateway takes bare names, and the
model family has to match the protocol path, so Claude models serve
`snow ai claude` and 503 on the OpenAI-style path OpenCode uses.

Also notes that the unit tests mock the connection and so cannot catch a
wrong credential or URL shape, and states what a live run has to cover.

* fix(ai): keep the mocked subprocess out of the config permission check

The ai tests patch commands.subprocess.run, but commands.subprocess is the
stdlib module itself, so that patch is process-wide - and
subprocess.check_output() is implemented on top of run(). On Windows the CLI
checks config-file permissions by shelling out to icacls via check_output,
which then received the mock's stdout, None, and raised TypeError in
re.finditer before the command under test ever ran. Ten tests failed on
windows-latest while passing on ubuntu, and fail-fast cancelled the Ubuntu job.

Reporting the config file as strict keeps that check away from subprocess
entirely, so the mock only ever sees the agent launch. Reproduced on macOS by
forcing IS_WINDOWS, which raises the identical TypeError before this change and
passes after it.

Also adds the `ai` command row to the e2e help snapshots, which assert the
top-level command list.

* fix(ai): narrow the agent subprocess patch instead of disabling a CLI check

The previous commit stopped the Windows failure by reporting the config file as
strict, which suppressed a real CLI code path rather than fixing the cause. The
process-wide patch stayed in place, so any other CLI path that shelled out
during these tests would have broken the same way.

The cause is the patch target. commands.subprocess is the stdlib module object,
so patching its run() applies process-wide, and subprocess.check_output() is
built on run(). Replacing the `subprocess` name in this plugin's namespace
confines the mock to this plugin: every other caller binds the module through
its own import and keeps the real one.

Verified that under the shipped helper an unrelated subprocess.check_output()
still returns real output, the Windows permission branch reaches real icacls
rather than the mock, and the agent launch is still intercepted.

* docs(ai): correct why the OpenCode provider needs an account

The docstring and README claimed a missing account makes the provider skip the
compatibility fetch wrapper. Reading the provider out of the OpenCode bundle
shows otherwise: account and the token are treated as one credential pair, and
with either missing the provider loads a stub whose getModel() raises "missing
credentials", so nothing is sent at all. The wrapper is gated on where the
credential came from - it is skipped only for OAuth-only credentials - so
passing apiKey is what attaches it, not account.

Also records that the value is deliberately not a Snowflake account identifier,
since the provider only uses it to interpolate a default baseURL that
options.baseURL overrides, and that SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT and
SNOWFLAKE_CORTEX_TOKEN/_PAT in the environment take precedence over this config.

No behaviour change.

* docs(ai): restore the correct reason the OpenCode provider needs an account

Reverts the previous commit's explanation, which was wrong. A live run without
an account produces "Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens'" from the gateway, not
the "missing credentials" error that commit described, so the account is what
gates the compat fetch wrapper exactly as originally documented: the provider
assembles its options, wrapper included, only past a guard that returns early
when no account is resolved, so the max_tokens rewrite never gets attached.

Records why the symptom is a model compatibility error rather than an auth
error: OpenCode falls back to a plain openai-compatible client built from the
supplied options, which has no wrapper.

Keeps the note added by that commit about SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT and
SNOWFLAKE_CORTEX_TOKEN/_PAT taking precedence over this config.

No behaviour change.

* fix(ai): address review - replace --gateway-url, standard attribution headers, tighten env

Review changes from #252.

Security, from @oskar-lorek_snow's blocking finding and @sumit-das's suggestion:

- **--gateway-url is replaced by --gateway-name** (default SNOWFLAKE). The host is
  always taken from the connection, so there is no longer any way to aim an agent
  at a caller-supplied host, and a private link connection reaches its own
  endpoint without configuration. The name is restricted to Snowflake identifier
  characters because it is interpolated into the URL path. The test that asserted
  a PAT could be sent to http://127.0.0.1 is replaced by tests asserting the host
  comes from the connection and that names carrying URL syntax are refused.
- **Conflicting environment is refused rather than silently honoured.** The agents
  read ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK/_USE_VERTEX, SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT
  and SNOWFLAKE_CORTEX_TOKEN/_PAT ahead of what this command passes, so leaving
  them set would authenticate with a credential whose authenticator was never
  validated, or route traffic off the gateway.
- **The OpenCode config is a SecretType**, unwrapped at its single point of use,
  so a stray log or traceback masks the embedded credential.
- The unverifiable-binary and unauthenticated-header properties are now stated in
  the code rather than left to be discovered.

Attribution now uses the headers sf-cli already sends and the gateway logs:
X-Snowflake-Application and X-Snowflake-Baggage, alongside snow-agent-name.
ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS is merged first-write-wins instead of overwritten, so a
parent process that set them keeps its values.

Telemetry is only requested from Claude Code when it is enabled for the
connection - the same switch that governs snow's own - and each variable is set
with setdefault, so a deliberate CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=0 is respected.

Process and docs:

- CODEOWNERS entries for the plugin and its tests, so future changes do not wait
  on the CLI team.
- The group is hidden from `snow --help` while the feature is in preview.
- README-AI-GATEWAY.md is deleted from src/ and replaced by docs/ai-gateway.md.
  Verified by building the wheel: everything under src/snowflake is packaged, so
  that file shipped to PyPI with a mitmproxy recipe, an internal branch name,
  connector private attribute names and an internal clone URL. The new doc drops
  the debugging section entirely, no longer suggests any command that prints a
  live token, and requires a least-privilege role plus a network policy.
- Corrected claims that were wrong in the safer-sounding direction: that
  overriding the URL could not send a token elsewhere, that OpenCode sends no
  custom header, that two authenticators are supported, and the OAuth section
  that filed a short credential lifetime as a defect.
- RELEASE-NOTES trimmed to a user-facing summary.
- Test assertions on option names strip ANSI, so colourised output cannot break a
  substring check.

* fix(ai): name the launcher snow-ai-cli in X-Snowflake-Application

snowflake-cli named the whole CLI, which makes `snow ai` traffic indistinguishable
from anything else snow might send through the gateway. snow-ai-cli identifies the
launcher specifically and matches the shape of the other registered values
(sf-ai-cursor, snowci-ai-foundation).

* fix(ai): keep snowflake-cli as the X-Snowflake-Application value

Reverts the previous commit. The header names the client, which is what snow
identifies itself as elsewhere. Which agent was launched is already carried
separately, in the X-Snowflake-Baggage agent.name key and in snow-agent-name, so
encoding it in the application value too was redundant.

* fix(ai): drop X-Snowflake-Baggage, the agent name header already carries it

The baggage payload only ever held {"agent.name": ...}, which snow-agent-name
already states directly. Two headers carrying one fact is redundant, and the
baggage key was picked by us rather than blessed by the gateway team.

Attribution is now X-Snowflake-Application (the client) plus snow-agent-name
(which agent was launched).

* fix(ai): stop refusing SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT, and correct stale rationale

SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT is a supported snow connection variable, so refusing it broke a
documented way of configuring the connection this command depends on - and it
could change neither the credential nor the endpoint, since the provider uses
account only for a default baseURL we override.

Also: drop the "deliberately narrow" framing that presented an implementation-effort
decision as a security one, state what the Claude telemetry variables do and which
of them is unverified, fix comments left stale by the baggage removal, report an
unreadable connection config instead of reporting it as an unset authenticator,
default telemetry to enabled when the connection cannot be inspected, and record
why the gateway name is not case-folded.

* fix: clean up rebase artifacts in release notes and help snapshots

The rebase onto main replayed the release-note edit from every commit that
touched it, leaving six stacked copies of the same bullet anchored in the
released v3.26.0 section rather than under Unreleased. Reduced to the single
current bullet and moved to Unreleased, since v3.26.0 and v3.27.0 were both
cut after this branch diverged.

Regenerated the help and e2e installation snapshots. Both carried two stale
"New version of Snowflake CLI available" banner lines that were recorded on
this branch when the version check happened to fire; main has none, so the
snapshots failed in isolation. Both snapshot files are now purely additive
against main.

* test(ai): refresh help snapshots for the new --format config hint

main now documents the env var and cli.output_format config key on the global
--format option, which appears in every command's help.

* docs(ai): make the PAT setup SQL actually run

CREATE USER PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKEN is not valid syntax; token creation is
ALTER USER <user> ADD PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKEN. Verified by compiling both
forms: the documented one fails with a syntax error.

Also bind the network policy to the user. Creating the policy had no effect on
its own, so the guide's own least-privilege advice did not take hold. Capitalise
the SNOWFLAKE gateway identifier, and note that the token secret is shown once.

* feat(ai): propagate OpenCode trace context while preserving exporter settings

Keep Claude credentials masked until subprocess handoff, retain the console exporter fallback, and include the CLI team in AI plugin ownership. Cover telemetry opt-out, exporter preservation, masking, and child-process credential handoff with regression tests.

### Pre-review checklist
   * [ ] If my changes add or modify user-facing interface (commands, flags, output formats), I consulted maintainers and got sign-off beforehand ([how](https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-cli/blob/main/docs/contributing/adding-commands.md#design-sign-off-before-writing-code)).
   * [x] I've confirmed that instructions included in README.md are still correct after my changes in the codebase.
   * [x] I've added or updated unit tests to verify correctness of my new code.
   * [ ] I've added or updated integration tests to verify correctness of my new code.
   * [x] Manually tested on macOS
   * [ ] Manually tested on Windows
   * [x] I've confirmed my changes are up-to-date with the target branch.
   * [x] No `RELEASE-NOTES.md` update (hidden maintainer flags only; PR has `skip-release-notes`).
   * [x] I've updated documentation if behavior changed.

## Summary

Consolidates maintainer doc generation onto a single hidden flag: `snow --docs` now produces command-reference MDX under `gen_docs/pages` and still regenerates project-definition reference under `gen_docs/project_definition`. Removes the hidden `snow --docs-pages` flag and updates `publish_command_docs.py` and contributor docs to invoke `--docs`.

This is **not** an end-user CLI change (`--docs` remains hidden and out of `--help`). It replaces the legacy `gen_docs/commands` usage-fragment output with full pages and deletes the unused usage-fragment generator code and Jinja templates.

## Test plan

- [x] `hatch run pytest tests/test_docs_generation_output.py tests/test_command_docs_coverage.py tests/scripts/test_publish_command_docs.py tests/test_main.py::test_docs_callback`
- [x] `hatch run pre-commit run --all-files`
- [ ] `hatch run python scripts/publish_command_docs.py --dry-run` (or local `snow --docs` smoke) before the next prod-docs publish

### Changes description

- `generate_docs()` calls `generate_command_pages` + `generate_project_definition_docs`; remove `generate_command_docs` and `usage.mdx.jinja2` / `overview.mdx.jinja2`.
- `cli_app.py`: remove `--docs-pages` eager option; broaden `--docs` help text.
- Contributing guides and publish scripts use `--docs`; tests renamed to match (`test_docs_*` vs `test_docs_pages_*`).

Add CommandDocs for snow app setup, run, publish, and version commands

### Pre-review checklist
   * [ ] If my changes add or modify user-facing interface (commands, flags, output formats), I consulted maintainers and got sign-off beforehand ([how](https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-cli/blob/main/docs/contributing/adding-commands.md#design-sign-off-before-writing-code)).

   * [ ] I've added or updated integration tests to verify correctness of my new code.
   * [x] Manually tested on macOS
   * [ ] Manually tested on Windows
   * [x] I've confirmed my changes are up-to-date with the target branch.
   * [ ] I've described my changes in `RELEASE-NOTES.md` (see [when and how](https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-cli/blob/main/docs/contributing/lifecycle.md#release-notes-format)).
   * [ ] I've updated documentation if behavior changed.

Sign-off: not applicable. No command, flag, or output changes for end users; this is docs-generation plumbing.
Release notes: skipped; internal docs machinery with no user-visible CLI change.
Integration tests: not applicable.

### Changes description

> [!WARNING]
> **`command_docs_paths.yaml` and `_COMMAND_DOCS_MIGRATION_PENDING_PATHS` are intentionally not updated in this PR.** Those changes are deferred to a follow-up PR so parallel command migrations can merge without YAML conflicts. Commands migrated here stay on the migration pending list until that follow-up lands.

- Add inline `CommandDocs` for six `snow app` commands: `setup` (Snowflake App Runtime), `run`, `publish`, and `version create` / `list` / `drop` (Native App), with prod-docs parity on usage notes, examples, and related links.
- Add `"native-app": "Snowflake Native App"` to `REFERENCE_TEXT` for `%native-app%` in publish usage notes.
- Related links are inlined on each command (no shared one-use helpers).
- Split multi-paragraph example prose into separate `Example` entries; prose-only lines use `command=""` (no `snowcli` block). `page.mdx.jinja2` and `docs_help.py` skip rendering when `command` is empty.

**Content policy:** match prod-docs usage notes, examples, and related links wherever `CommandDocs` can render them. Known generator deltas: list-item `-` prefix on examples, `bash` → `snowcli` on run's first example, `**V1**` → plain `V1`.

**Page intro:** the text between `` and `## Syntax` comes from the command docstring / `help=` (not `CommandDocs`).

**How to read the MDX diffs below**

One collapsible per command shows the **full-page** unified diff from **prod-docs** → generated MDX. **`-` lines** are prod today; **`+` lines** are generator output.

Most Syntax/Options deltas are shared CLI flag churn rather than app-specific rewrites.

### Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_command_docs_coverage.py`
- [x] `pytest tests/test_help_messages.py -k "app and (setup or run or publish or version)"` (help snapshots unchanged when `ENABLE_COMMAND_DOCS_IN_HELP` is off — CI default)
- [x] `snow --docs-pages` for app command mappings
- [x] pre-commit on touched files

- Bootstraps app.yml for Snowflake App Runtime; usage notes and deploy follow-up examples.

### Changes description

Stacked on #386. When `ENABLE_CONDENSED_COMMAND_HELP` is enabled, per-command help is shorter by collapsing the large global and connection option panels into a compact summary.

- Add `CondensedHelp` mixin on `SnowTyperCommand` and `SortedTyperGroup`.
- Default `snow <cmd> --help`: command-specific options only, plus a condensed shared-options panel (flag names, no descriptions) and usage suffixes `[global options]` / `[connection options]`.
- `snow --help`: append full global and connection option panels (moved out of per-command help).
- Hidden `--help-all` on commands with injected options: restores legacy full per-command help.
- Reject `--help` and `--help-all` together.
- Always use `SnowTyperCommand` for decorated commands (not only when `CommandDocs` is present).
- Fix root `--help` wiring: `callback=self._help_callback()` (was missing `()`, so shared panels never rendered).
- When `ENABLE_CONDENSED_COMMAND_HELP` is off, reject `--help-all` as an unknown option so the default-off path is a strict no-op (`bd73fa3`).

### Design choices

**Three help surfaces, one source of truth.**

| Invocation | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| `snow <cmd> --help` | Command options + condensed shared-option names + footer |
| `snow <cmd> --help-all` | Legacy full help (all panels, full descriptions) |
| `snow --help` | Top-level commands + full global/connection panels |

Shared options are documented once at the root; per-command help focuses on what differs per command.

**Hide params, don't fork Click/Typer rendering.** During condensed help we temporarily set `hidden=True` on injected options, call the normal `format_help`, then restore visibility in a `finally` block.

**Usage suffix gated by `_condensed_help_active`.** `[global options]` / `[connection options]` append only during condensed `format_help`, not for `--help-all` or when the flag is off.

**`--help-all` as a hidden eager global option.** Injected via `GLOBAL_OPTIONS` with `expose_value=False` and `is_eager=True`.

**`invocation_args` in `parse_args`.** Stores argv on `ctx.obj` so `--help` / `--help-all` conflict detection works regardless of ordering.

**Condensed panel = names only.** Descriptions live on `snow --help` or `--help-all`. Footer points reviewers to those entry points.

**`CommandDocs` panels unchanged.** When `ENABLE_COMMAND_DOCS_IN_HELP` is on, usage notes / examples / related topics still render after condensed help.

**PrPr / feature flag.** Default off, no release note. Unit tests use `@with_feature_flags`.

### Review follow-up

- Gated `--help-all` on `ENABLE_CONDENSED_COMMAND_HELP` in `handle_help_all_option` (`bd73fa3`); added `test_condensed_help_flag_off_rejects_help_all`.
- Leaf-only `--help-all` (via `GLOBAL_OPTIONS` on commands) is intentional for this PrPr; group/root can be revisited later if we want one flag everywhere.

description:
Allow integer in filters

* Allow integer in filters

Closes #16419

Took a Claude stab at resolving #16418

### Problem

Users using v2 are unable to use Jinja filters where the attribute arg is an integer. See example in #16418

### Solution

The `map` filter already handled both kinds of argument correctly. I reused its approach rather than writing a new one:

1. **Read `attribute` as any value**, not only a string.
2. **Look it up based on its type** with a shared helper, `get_attr`:
   - a string is looked up by name or dotted path, as before (`"name"`, `"a.0"`)
   - anything else, like an integer, is looked up by position (`0`, `1`)
3. **Use a second helper, `get_attr_or_default`,** for filters that fall back to a default when the lookup fails or finds nothing. It replaces the old `get_path_or_default`, which only took strings; I removed that since nothing uses it any more.

### Checklist

- [x] I have read [the contributing guide](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and understand what's expected of me.

feat(wizard): sign in through a dbt account host (SSO escape hatch)

* feat(dbt-platform-auth): log in through an account host's /oauth/authorize

Interactive login always opened https://us1.dbt.com/register. That page
cannot route SSO users whose account lives on another deployment: it
cannot find their account or SSO connection, rejects their email as
already registered, and they loop.

Add a login host override (builder `login_host` / `login_account_id`,
env `DBT_CLOUD_LOGIN_HOST` / `DBT_CLOUD_LOGIN_ACCOUNT_ID`). When set, the
flow opens standard OAuth at `https://{host}/oauth/authorize`, which
applies the account's own login (including SSO). The callback from that
endpoint carries no `account_url`, so the code is exchanged at the login
host with the unmodified `redirect_uri`, passing `account_id` when given.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* feat(wizard): accept a dbt login host in the wizard login server

Thread `login_host` / `login_account_id` through `DbtPlatformServerOptions`
into the dbt platform OAuth resolver, so wizard logins can skip the
registration page and authenticate on the account host. Unset options
fall back to `DBT_CLOUD_LOGIN_HOST` / `DBT_CLOUD_LOGIN_ACCOUNT_ID`, which
is the escape hatch for the Wizard CLI.

The mock OAuth server gains an `/oauth/authorize` route that, like the
real endpoint, reads `redirect_uri` and returns no `account_url`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* feat(wizard): persist a dbt login host and use it at every sign-in

Store `providers.dbt.login_host` / `login_account_id` in providers.json and
pass them to the dbt Platform login server from the app server, `wizard
login`, and `wizard provider configure`, so each opens the account host's
/oauth/authorize instead of us1 /register. The desktop app gets a
`dbt_platform_set_login_override` command and sees the saved values in
`provider_show`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* feat(wizard): add an advanced dbt sign-in host to Configure dbt

The Configure dbt dialog gets a collapsible "Advanced sign-in" section with
a dbt account host and optional account ID. The values are saved on Save
and before "Sign in with dbt platform" starts, so a user whose account is
on another deployment can sign in on its Access URL instead of the us1
registration page.

A signed-out dbt row now offers "Sign-in options", which opens the dialog;
before, the only control started the browser sign-in directly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 

* feat(wizard): set the dbt login host from the Wizard CLI and TUI

Add `dbt-wizard providers dbt set-login-host  [--account-id ]`
and `clear-login-host`, and a "Set sign-in host" entry in the TUI
`/providers` dbt details popup (host prompt, then an optional account ID),
so CLI and TUI users can save `providers.dbt.login_host` without the
desktop app or an env var. Both validate through
`normalize_dbt_login_override`, same as the app.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5

description:
fix(kernels): stream kernels output files through download_file (#1206)

## Summary

`kaggle kernels output` now saves each file through `download_file`, the
path dataset and competition downloads already take. Files are written
in chunks instead of held in memory, checked against Content-Length, and
resumed after a dropped connection.

## Problem

`kernels_output` fetches each file with `requests.get(url, stream=True)`
and writes `response.content`, which reads the whole body into memory.
The request has no read timeout, nothing retries it, and nothing
compares the written size with Content-Length. The target file is opened
before the body is read, so when the connection drops, the command fails
and leaves an empty file under the final name.

Measured with an in-process HTTP server (macOS arm64, Python 3.14,
requests 2.34.2):

| case | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 512 MiB output: growth of the client's peak RSS | 1,175 MB | 7 MB |
| 3 MiB output, connection cut after 1.5 MiB | `ChunkedEncodingError`,
0-byte file left on disk | resumed from the first 1 MiB chunk, all
3,145,728 bytes written |

## Solution

Call `download_file` for kernel output files and pass `timeout=300` to
the first request, the same read timeout `download_file` uses for its
retries. Resume is on unless `--force` is given, as in `datasets
download`.

`download_file` does not use its `http_client` argument, and the client
opened for the output listing is closed by the time the files are
fetched, so the call passes `None`.

## Tests

- New `tests/unit/test_kernels_output_download.py` runs `kernels_output`
against a local HTTP server that supports Range requests. One test
checks that the file goes through `download_file` and arrives intact.
The other cuts the first connection halfway through the second 1 MiB
chunk and checks that the retry asks for `bytes=1048576-` and that no
`.kaggle-partial` marker is left. Both fail on main.
- `test_kernels_output_paths.py` and two pagination tests in
`test_kernels_logs.py` faked the old `.content` read. They now stub
`download_file`, and the `requests.get` assertion includes the timeout.

`pytest tests/unit`: 1397 passed. `black --check` and `mypy` report no
issues.

description:
feat(app-server): serve MCP statelessly from the Worker

The session Durable Objects were the bottleneck and most of the cost.
They held every session's McpServer + transport in memory; with the
per-session tag map they hit the 128 MB limit ~1,200 times an hour all
September (resetting and dropping every session) and overloaded outright
on 2026-09-30. The 16-shard hotfix cured that but multiplied the billed
DO duration ~6x. Most sessions are Claude.ai connector refreshes
(initialize, tools/list, resources/list, never a DELETE), and the only
state a session needs is whether its client renders the app.

Now every /mcp request gets its own server and transport in the Worker:

- initialize mints the session id as ui- or noui- from the
  declared io.modelcontextprotocol/ui capability, and later requests
  read it back through createServer's new uiSession option - which also
  ends the lost detection on re-created sessions, which never saw the
  initialize
- the other signal, the client fetching the app resource, lives in a
  per-session MCPSessionManager object (RPC + storage, dropped by a 24 h
  alarm) that only clients without the declaration reach
- GET answers 405 (no standalone SSE stream), DELETE 200; session-less
  non-initialize requests keep the transport's 400, which 2026-07-28
  clients' server/discover probes fall back from
- /health runs an initialize through the same path
- the shape-search tag map is built on the first search, not per server

The Node server keeps its per-session servers and is unaffected. Tested
with wrangler dev and on staging: raw HTTP checks, the SDK client,
claude-code 2.1.284 (probe + fallback) and codex 0.155.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
product_or_resource: feat(app-server): serve MCP statelessly from the Worker

description:
feat(app-server): add a /health endpoint for uptime monitors

Pingdom counts any 4xx as down and can't be told otherwise, so the 400
"Session not found" of a session-less GET /mcp can't serve as the probe,
and POSTing a real initialize would open a session on every check.

The Worker routes /health to a random shard the same way it routes that
GET, and the Durable Object answers 200 "ok" before any session logic -
so the check covers the DOs (it would have caught today's overload)
without creating a session. The Node server answers /health directly,
for container health checks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
product_or_resource: feat(app-server): add a /health endpoint for uptime monitors

description:
fix(app-server): stop overloading the session Durable Objects

Production answered /mcp with 500s and 25 s timeouts on 2026-09-30:
"Durable Object is overloaded. Requests queued for too long." About 20
requests per second, 88% of them new sessions, were landing on 4 session
Durable Objects, and a DO works through its requests one at a time.

Every new session built its own search_shapes tag map over the
10,446-shape index: ~50-110 ms of CPU and a full copy in memory, inside
the DO, on every initialize. The map is read-only after the build, so it
is now built once per index and shared - createServer drops to under a
millisecond after the first session.

And the shard count goes from 4 to 16, the most the first-hex-char
routing allows. Sessions whose id now maps to another shard are
re-created there transparently by the existing stale-session path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
product_or_resource: fix(app-server): stop overloading the session Durable Objects

description:
fix: image-block 'Copy Image' and 'Show file in folder' context menu actions (#13552)

* fix: 'Copy Image' context menu action

The native right-click 'Copy Image' resolved the image srcURL with a raw 'subs 7' and nativeImage.createFromPath, which only works for bare POSIX file:/// URLs: any URI-encoded path (e.g. a graph directory containing spaces -> %20), https/blob/data srcURLs and Windows paths produced an empty image and silently wrote nothing to the clipboard. Use webContents.copyImageAt(x, y) instead, which copies the rendered image for any source.

Also fix the asset 'Copy image' action: for http(s) image sources read-file-raw is not a filesystem path and failed silently; fall back to the fetch/ClipboardItem path (same as web), and surface a 'Can't find file' toast instead of a console-only error when the local file is missing.

* fix: 'Show file in folder' context menu actions

The image action-bar item routed on the 'local?' link flag: non-local sources (file://, absolute /path, ~ paths) were sent to shell.openExternal, which throws 'illegal protocol' for non-http(s) URLs and relative paths - a silent no-op, with a misleading 'Open image in browser' label for what is actually a local file. Route on whether the resolved image-src is an http(s) URL instead: remote sources open in the browser, everything else reveals via openFileInFolder, labeled 'Show file in folder'.

Both reveal entry points (image action bar and block context menu) also silently did nothing when the file was missing or the path was unresolved (missing download, plugin-sourced asset under assets/storages/). Check the file exists first and show a 'Can't find file' toast; resolve plugin-sourced asset paths from the asset's external-url the same way the renderer does.

* fix: decode protected Windows drive colon in url-to-path

assets:// URLs protect a Windows drive colon as /logseq__colon/; the
renderer-side decoder in url-to-path never restored it, so the
resolved path stayed encoded instead of a native C:/ path.

* fix: reveal absolute-path external-url in folder

The block menu resolved a non-local-relative external-url to the
block's uuid path, so an absolute path or file:// URL revealed a
non-existent file.

* fix: render local filesystem image paths on Electron

Local filesystem image hrefs resolved against the app origin and 404d.
Route ~/, file://, absolute, and graph-relative (./ ../ bare) paths
through assets:// URLs; bare http(s) URLs and web behavior unchanged.

* fix: match http image sources case-insensitively

URL schemes are case-insensitive; an uppercase HTTPS:// src was
misclassified as a local file path for copy and reveal.

* fix: keep http and root-relative image links in image-link

Routing every non-asset href through assets:// on Electron mangled
uppercase HTTP:// links into graph paths, and reordering publishing
before the ~ / check stripped the root slash from published images.
Match the scheme case-insensitively and restore the leading ~ /
branch ahead of the publishing rewrite; Electron still resolves both
to assets:// URLs.

* fix: pass protocol-relative image links through unchanged

//host/path is a remote URL, not a filesystem path; the Electron
assets:// resolution was mangling it.

* feat: show asset action bar on inline images in Electron

Inline ![](path) images have no asset entity, so the dots menu never
rendered. Show it on Electron whenever the image src resolves, and
keep Align/Delete gated on the asset entity.

* fix: classify inline image actions by URL scheme

data:/blob:// image-src values were sent down the filesystem copy
path and got a folder-reveal item that could never resolve. Treat
image-src as a file only when it has no scheme and no // prefix
(C:/ stays a Windows path, not a scheme), and hide the
reveal/browser item when neither applies.

* fix: close added when/let around image menu reveal item

* add external assets comment

* fix: classify // by original src, keeping UNC paths as files

assets://server/share unwraps to //server/share in image-src;
checking src for the // prefix keeps UNC files on the filesystem
path while raw //host hrefs still count as remote.

---------

Co-authored-by: Tienson Qin

description:
feat(enums): align enums with OpenAPI specs and deprecate removed members (#789)

Update the trading and broker enums to match the current Trading and
Broker OpenAPI specs. Members the next release will remove, or will
rename, stay available but emit a DeprecationWarning.

Deprecation mechanism

Add DeprecatingEnumMeta (alpaca/_deprecating_enum.py), an EnumMeta
subclass. It emits a DeprecationWarning (stacklevel=2) when a listed
member is accessed:
- by attribute (Enum.NAME)
- by name (Enum["NAME"])
- by value (Enum("wire_value")) for removed members only

Looking a member up by value still returns it, so old payloads keep
parsing. Nothing warns on import, class creation, or iteration, or for
members that are not deprecated. Equality and .value are unchanged.
Deprecation messages live in maps at module level, because a dict in
the class body would become an enum member on Python 3.10.

ActivityType
- Add CGD, DIVFEE, DIVFT, DIVTW, FOPT, INTNRA, INTTW, JNL, MISC, OPCA,
  PTR, REO, TRANS.
- Deprecate DIVWH, EXTRD, FXTRD, INTPNL, SWP, VOF, WH. None of them
  appear in either the Trading or the Broker spec.
- Keep CIL, MEM, CFEE and NC, which are still in the Broker spec.

OrderStatus
- Deprecate PENDING_REVIEW.

OrderClass
- Add EMPTY ("").

OrderSide
- Add BUY_MINUS, SELL_PLUS, SELL_SHORT, SELL_SHORT_EXEMPT, UNDISCLOSED,
  CROSS, CROSS_SHORT (Broker spec).

AssetClass
- Add TREASURY, CORPORATE, GLOBAL_EQUITY, US_INDEX, US_EQUITY_CHAIN,
  IPO.

AssetExchange
- Deprecate ASCX, CBSE, ERSX, FTXU, GNSS.

AccountStatus
- Add ACCOUNT_CLOSED_PENDING.
- Deprecate AML_REVIEW, DISABLED, DISABLE_PENDING, EDITED,
  KYC_SUBMITTED, REAPPROVAL_PENDING, RESUBMITTED, SIGNED_UP.

AgreementType (broker)
- Add MARGIN_AGREEMENT, ACCOUNT_AGREEMENT, CUSTOMER_AGREEMENT,
  CRYPTO_AGREEMENT and OPTIONS_AGREEMENT as the canonical names.
- MARGIN, ACCOUNT, CUSTOMER, CRYPTO and OPTIONS become deprecated
  aliases of the new names. Access by attribute or by name warns;
  lookup by wire value does not, because those values are still valid.
- Deprecate CUSTODIAL_CUSTOMER, which the Broker spec no longer lists.

Other broker enums
- AccountType: add TRUST, OMNIBUS_NON_DISCLOSED, OMNIBUS_SUB, JOINT.
- ACHRelationshipStatus: add REJECTED, CANCEL_REQUESTED.
- BankAccountType: deprecate NONE ("").
- BankStatus: add REJECTED.
- TransferStatus: deprecate SETTLED.
- JournalStatus: add ACTIVITY_CREATED.

Tests
- Removed members warn on all three lookups and still return the
  member.
- Renamed AgreementType aliases warn on attribute and name lookups,
  resolve to the canonical member, and lookup by wire value does not
  warn.
- Neighboring stable members and newly added values do not warn.
- Importing the enum modules emits no deprecation warning.
- The broker account factory now uses the new AgreementType names.

Fixes #682
Supersedes #784

description:
本版本将已交付的 v1.0.63-beta.3 晋级正式版，汇总本版本线三个 beta 的变化，并纳入下方列出的 beta 后变更。

Added

  • 数字员工 — 新增管理、能力资源、运行追踪、员工身份登录与本地 Agent/DSH 接入；支持草稿、发布、Skill ZIP 上传与员工域 MCP 配置，使用 agentUuid / userId 身份契约。草稿配置与发布分别执行，事件连接状态区分 IPC、Agent 初始化和实际传输就绪。
  • 通讯录与邮箱查人 — 支持通过 dingtalkId 查询 userId，通过企业邮箱单个或批量查询员工；批量查询分别保留已成功、未找到、失败与未知结果，避免把未确认结果报告为未找到。
  • 考勤审批与鉴权快照 — 增加审批时长计算、出差/外出配套日程校验及复杂加班设置查询；auth status --readonly 提供不联网、不刷新、不写凭据的本地状态快照。
  • 等待能力 — 框架增加声明式轮询、事件与自动回退等待；声明支持的命令提供 --wait / --wait-timeout，超时保留 pending 与最后观察状态，事件与轮询共用截止时间。
  • 白板与 AI 表格恢复 — 增加白板 SVG 预览、差异确认、个人/团队及模板中心模板；AI 表格提供只读写入结果查询及保留原 clientToken 的不确定写入恢复路径。

Changed

  • Schema 与启动性能 — 每次执行保持完整 Cobra 命令树，减少元数据和初始化分配；支持平台在安装或首次使用时从本机声明生成身份及经过认证的持久缓存。缓存缺失或损坏时修复，运行时插件场景由隔离子进程完成缓存构建与修复。
  • 消息读取与国际登录 — 智能消息读取在策略允许时解密第三方加密消息，保留逐项解密台账；MCP 与输出投影保留大整数精度。国际登录默认使用英文，国内登录沿用现有语言设置。
  • 数字员工参数与文档 — 主程序类型统一使用 --type，可见范围使用 --user-ids，保留历史参数兼容；支持可选创建提示词、发布本地员工前按需初始化提示词，以及草稿文本的空值校验。更新 OA TableField 二维数组示例、Devapp/Devdoc 流程及文档列表路由。
  • 参数错误 — 框架统一参数校验的错误分类与退出码，保留业务错误及取消/超时的原有语义。
  • AI 搜问证据 — 丰富搜索结果的证据与解析详情，使用说明要求先核对证据再给出结论或交接后续操作。

Fixed

  • 跨平台发布 — 修复 Windows SafeChat CGO 运行库崩溃，以及 Darwin amd64 产物被 dyld 拒绝启动的问题；Darwin 构建固定 macOS 11.0 最低目标，签名资产验收检查 SG_READ_ONLY 并实际启动可执行的 Darwin 产物。
  • AI 表格回执与分页 — 表单分享按返回身份、显式请求字段和 CP 同步状态验证结果；未完整确认时保留部分失败证据。未知写入不重放创建；失效游标丢弃旧快照结果，复合流程停止后续写入。配套恢复接口仍依赖对应 MCP 服务与网关部署。
  • 登录恢复 — 缺失 DEK 或旧密文不匹配时允许重新登录，取得新凭据后才替换目标；登录中的临时身份查询立即使用本次 MCP 端点覆盖，保留刷新及暂时 Keychain 故障的保护。
  • 消息与事件 — 修复单聊引用回复的误拒绝，保留 OA 审批事件业务字段；个人 Stream 正确响应系统控制帧，数字员工连接沿用事件来源默认规则，改进重连及 Windows 正常停止判断。
  • 文件与凭据边界 — 数字员工 Skill ZIP 使用同一已打开句柄完成校验与上传，防止路径替换；补充失败清理、绑定回执和日志脱敏验证。

Removed

  • 旧合同审查入口 — 隐藏历史 contract review benefit|create|analysis|result 命令并标记不可用；保留历史参数入口，但以 command_retired 拒绝执行，不再调用旧 MCP。

Changes since v1.0.63-beta.3

Added

  • Add dws aicard explain , lint, and preview. The embedded DingTalk A2UI protocol supports native offline lookup and structural validation without Python. Preview validates a complete new-card file and sends it to the current user's direct chat; dry-run does not send. Include the DWS authoring Skill and report request acceptance separately from client-rendering evidence.

  • Drive & Wiki set-share-scope — add dws drive permission set-share-scope and dws wiki permission set-share-scope for managing node-level and workspace-level share visibility (PRIVATE / ORGANIZATION / PUBLIC) with partial-update semantics, role control, partner inclusion, organization search/recommend toggles, password protection and expiration (drive node only).

  • OA 审批模板创建与更新命令 — 新增 dws oa approval template create（oa/create_process_template）与 dws oa approval template update（oa/update_process_template），均为企业钉钉管理员能力。两者支持逐项参数模式（create 必填 --name、--schema-content；update 必填 --process-code、--name、--schema-content、--process-config），也支持 --from-document 传入完整 JSON 文档的绝对路径整体配置，两种模式互斥；--schema-content、--process-config 等对象参数以 JSON 字符串发送给 MCP，--plugin-configs、--visible-range、--manager-user-ids 以数组发送，均支持直接 JSON、@文件 与 - 标准输入。CLI 侧做本地校验：schemaContent 控件 props.id 唯一性检查（递归进 children 嵌套控件）与 processConfig 结构校验，并解析 MCP 返回的 810001（同名模板冲突）/810002（模板数量超限）拒绝码为失败输出而非静默重试；--dry-run 仅做本地校验并展示请求参数（executed=false），成功统一由 data.processCode 返回模板编码。构造 processConfig 时若未显式指定审批人类型，审批节点默认使用部门主管（target_management）而非直属主管。Skill 文档：新增 oa-template-write.md（从 oa.md 拆分模板写入路由，渐进披露）与连接器审批人规则 target_connect_approval.md，并补充 50+ 个控件 schema、流程节点、选人规则子文档；oa.md 增加模板管理路由条目、process-nodes.md 增加连接器审批人条目、SKILL.md 引用 oa-template-write.md。验证状态：变更代码含完整单测（含 schema_oa_template_contract_test.go Schema 契约测试）与 mono-multi-coverage.yaml 的 oa-template-write 注册；模板名称是否可用、数量是否超限由创建 MCP 校验，dry-run 不能证明名称可用，建议创建/更新后再用 template detail 核对实际状态。

  • AI 表格访问密钥 — 新增 SQL Sheet API Key 的创建、查询和撤销命令，以及对应的 Agent 使用说明；完整凭据仅创建时返回，创建结果未知时先查询状态。

Changed

  • Git hooks 改为通过 make setup-hooks 显式启用，提交前仅检查暂存区格式与空白，不修改工作区。
  • 发布辅助脚本在退出时可靠清理临时目录和锁，并为下载增加有界重试、超时和阶段诊断。

Fixed

  • 固定 AI 卡片协议 JSON 的 Git 检出换行为 LF，修复 Windows 自动转换 CRLF 后协议哈希校验失败、卡片查询和校验命令无法使用的问题。

  • 修复 Windows 鉴权文件替换遇到短暂文件占用时的失败，保留旧文件并对受限错误执行有界重试。

  • 修复 Linux Skill 安装期间的目录身份校验，固定目录句柄并在结束后释放。

  • 修复产品命令根名称与产品 ID 不一致时的 Schema 缓存定位。

  • AI 听记整包导出支持服务端明确成功的空摘要，仍保留分析等待器的严格判断。

  • 钉钉招聘创建职位时正确处理校园招聘默认值，并保留 Connector 返回的业务错误信息。

Security

  • Password argv sanitization — add --password to the timing/perf report sensitive-flag allowlist so SanitizeCommand redacts it in both --password and --password= forms. This also fixes a pre-existing plaintext leak where dws drive publish set --password … wrote the raw secret into the DWS_PERF_REPORT argv record. The drive permission set-share-scope --dry-run preview now masks the password value as *** while still emitting requirePassword; real calls keep sending the correct secret and no business RPC is issued during preview.

description:
Added

  • Added message.send.save-copy, the mailbox a sent message is copied to when --save is not passed, and --no-save on message send, compose, reply and forward to skip it.

    It takes a mailbox name, alias or role, and the v1 true still reads as the sent mailbox. Leave it unset on Gmail and Microsoft Graph, which file the sent message themselves.

  • Added envelope.list.datetime-relative, rendering recent dates relative to today: the time for today, yesterday, then the weekday for the past week, older dates falling back to datetime-fmt ([#510]).

  • Added proxy, a per-account SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy every network backend connects through, and .proxy to override it for one backend ([#742]).

    The password is a secret like any credential, so it stays out of the URL. Without either, the all_proxy and https_proxy environment variables are still read.

  • Added --posting-style none to message reply and message forward, sending the written body without quoting the source.

  • Added a decoded template to message compose, message reply and message forward under --json when neither saving nor sending.

    It carries from, to, cc, bcc, subject and a body without the signature, so an editor can lay the message out and hand it back through the flags.

  • Added messages-added-details to gmail history list --json, preserving each arrival's message id, optional thread id and supplied label ids alongside the existing message-id arrays.

  • Added message add on Gmail, inserting the raw message through messages.insert with the mailbox and flags as labels, dated by its Date: header.

  • Added envelope search on Microsoft Graph, its filter translated to a KQL $search. Flag clauses are refused, Graph accepting no $filter beside $search, and the sort applies within the page.

  • A pimdir write now shows on the next read instead of on the next sync.

    A pimdir store is a replica the sync engine owns, so Himalaya appends its writes to the store's queue rather than apply them. A read used to project the committed index alone, so flagging a message lost the flag from the listing until Neverest ran.

    Reads now overlay the pending queue, so a staged flag, edit, deletion, move or copy shows straight away. All of them address a message that already exists and keeps its public id, so nothing changed about how a message is addressed.

    A staged creation has no id until the sync engine applies it, so it can be no envelope and does not list. envelope list reports how many the mailbox has and where to see them, and envelope search reports none, a queued message never having been matched against the query.

  • himalaya pimdir queue list and himalaya pimdir queue cancel, for the staged creations the mailbox listing cannot show.

    The pimdir binary is kind-agnostic and prints ids, hashes and flags. Himalaya holds the mail conventions and the blobs, so it renders a queued message with its flags, subject, recipient and the moment it was queued.

    cancel retracts one by the row id that view prints, which is the only way back for a message that does not exist yet: a staged flag or move is undone by doing the opposite.

    Cancelling is the store owner's write, so it takes that role for the length of the call and reports a sync in flight rather than wait on it.

  • Added sending from a pimdir account: the message is queued in the store for its owner to send, the one holding the credentials.

    The row is filed under the --save mailbox, else under mailbox.alias.sent, and shows in pimdir queue list. The command prints its row id, queueId under --json, which pimdir queue cancel takes and the owner reports against.

  • Added ManageSieve support behind the sieve cargo feature, on by default ([#739]).

    An account gains an optional [sieve] block, and himalaya sieve exposes capability, list, get, put, check, activate, deactivate, rename, delete and raw.

    The protocol lives in the new io-managesieve library, so every SASL mechanism the other backends accept works here too, and a password or a bearer token is refused over an unencrypted connection unless sieve.allow-cleartext-auth says otherwise.

    A bare sieve.server authority takes sieve:// with STARTTLS on, where the imap and smtp ones take their implicit-TLS scheme: RFC 5804 registers one port, 4190, and reaches TLS on it through STARTTLS.

    sieves:// is accepted for the deployments listening for a handshake straight away, and unix:// for a local pre-authenticated proxy.

  • Added the mailbox role (inbox, sent, drafts, trash...) to mailbox list, as a ROLE column and a role JSON field, with the mailbox.list.table.role-color option. [#743]

    JMAP reads the mailbox roles, Gmail its system labels and Graph its well-known folders, resolved in one $batch request. IMAP marks the inbox alone until SPECIAL-USE is read, and Maildir, m2dir and pimdir mark none. A mailbox.alias. entry overrides the role the backend reports.

  • Added imap fetch --body, fetching the whole message of every UID in the sequence set over one session (BODY.PEEK[], \Seen left unset) ([#762]).

    Downloading a mailbox took one message read per message, so one login per message, which some providers cut off after a dozen in a row. The JSON body field carries the octets as standard Base64, declared as such in the JSON Schema; the plain output prints the size only.

  • Added the mbox backend, behind the mbox cargo feature (off by default), over the new io-mbox library ([#697]).

    An mbox block points at a directory of mbox files and, optionally, at the spool ($MAIL) shown as INBOX. The shared commands read and write it, and himalaya mbox exposes the raw file operations. Any mbox file also opens by passing its absolute path as the mailbox. Writes lock the file the way MTAs and MUAs do, flags live in the Status and X-Status headers mutt and Dovecot use, and an index kept under the XDG cache directory makes a listing read only what changed.

Changed

  • Saving and sending at once (--save with --send, message send --save, message add --send) now sends first, so a failed send leaves no copy behind. A save failing after the send reports that the message was sent.

  • A pimdir account sends through the store's queue and no longer uses its smtp section. Behaviour change.

  • -m/--mailbox resolves a role after the aliases, so -m sent reaches the sent mailbox without an alias. A role carried by several mailboxes is an error naming them.

  • An omitted -m/--mailbox falls back to the inbox role when no inbox alias is set, instead of failing.

  • message delete takes the trash from mailbox.alias.trash first, then from the backend. Behaviour change: an alias set on JMAP, Gmail or Graph used to be ignored.

  • The wizard no longer pre-fills mailbox.alias.*, the backends reporting their roles themselves.

  • Changed Gmail draft create/update JSON output to structured draft, message and thread IDs, with schemas for both commands. Text confirmations are unchanged.

  • Changed the default --format of gmail messages get, gmail drafts get and gmail threads get from full to metadata.

    None of them prints more than metadata returns (id, labels, snippet, headers), so their output is unchanged, and Gmail no longer sends bodies that were thrown away. Pass --format full to get a thread's MIME payloads.

  • Forwarded vendored to io-pimdir and turned it on by default, so cargo install builds SQLite from source and needs none on the machine. Drop it to link the system SQLite and save about 1 MB; it also vendors OpenSSL when native-tls is on. The Nix builds still link the store's SQLite.

  • BREAKING: a pimdir store written before io-pimdir 0.4 is refused, and Himalaya reads the store's typed summaries.

    io-replica is retired, its sync engine folded into io-pimdir, and the store format moved with it: summaries are typed rows rather than a JSON meta column, and a store from the earlier draft is refused on open, saying to delete it and let Neverest resync. There is no migration, the draft offering none.

    An envelope now carries every From and To address with its display name, the In-Reply-To list and whether the message holds an attachment, straight from the store, and envelope list follows the store's newest-first order. A queued creation is rendered from the body it pins, the queued action carrying no summary any more.

  • A credential command that several blocks of one account name is now spawned once per run instead of once per block.

    account check and the wizard connection tests open IMAP, SMTP and ManageSieve in a row, each block resolving its own credential, so a pass or gpg entry was unlocked as many times as it was named. They now share one resolver, so it unlocks once.

    Two commands count as one only where the configuration wrote them identically: a shell line and the argv spelling of it stay distinct. A run reaching a single backend is unchanged.

  • BREAKING: a pimdir mailbox is now its collection id, verbatim, and pimdir.namespace is removed.

    -m imap/INBOX is what -m INBOX used to be, and a listing shows imap/INBOX in both columns.

    The sync engine binds a source's collections under a namespace, and Himalaya used to strip it back off, so one mailbox answered to two spellings. The store cannot be asked where that prefix ends: a collection id is opaque to it and hierarchy is a parent link rather than a separator.

    The stripping was therefore a guess at the sync engine's convention, needing a config key wherever it could not decide. The id is now the only spelling, as it already is for JMAP's opaque ids, and mailbox.alias.inbox = "imap/INBOX" is how you stop typing it.

  • Renamed the plural commands that name no vendor resource to their singular, the plural staying as a hidden alias.

    imap flags, maildir messages, maildir flags, m2dir messages and m2dir flags become imap flag, maildir message, maildir flag, m2dir message and m2dir flag. Every old spelling keeps working, hidden from --help.

    A command mirroring a vendor API resource keeps that API's spelling instead, so the gmail family is unchanged.

    The msgraph one, singular where Graph is plural, is aligned onto Graph: mail-folder, message and attachment become mail-folders, messages and attachments, joining the child-folders that already sat under the first.

    Every singular spelling stays as a hidden alias, where it used to be shown beside the plural, and completion, manual and json-schema gain the plural aliases they lacked.

  • Renamed the type configure prints from GeneratedConfig to ConfigureOutput, the shape the rest of the family uses.

    What the command prints is unchanged. Only the title of the himalaya-configure JSON Schema follows the new name.

Removed

  • Removed the mbox alias of the mailbox command: himalaya mbox now runs the new mbox backend command. Scripts should call the command by its name, himalaya mailbox, rather than by an alias.

Fixed

  • Fixed a message sent over JMAP staying in the drafts mailbox as a draft.

    The submission now asks the server to move it to the sent mailbox, unset $draft and set $seen once sent (RFC 8621 section 7.5 onSuccessUpdateEmail). The sent mailbox is the sent-role one, or the new jmap.sent-mailbox-id; without either, the message only loses $draft.

  • Fixed a successful IMAP append being reported as failed when its UID could not be recovered ([#759]).

    A server may acknowledge APPEND without APPENDUID, even with UIDPLUS, and some (QQ Exmail) also rewrite the Message-ID the fallback search looks for. The save now succeeds with an unknown id, and message add --json can return "id": null.

  • Fixed the "No backend matching auto" error saying nothing of the cause ([#740]). It now names the account and either the supported backends this build compiles in or the missing block, and points at MIGRATION.md when the account still carries the v1 backend table.

  • Fixed envelope list and envelope search truncating the ID column under --max-width.

    A long id, such as a Maildir file name, came out cut with an ellipsis and was unusable by any follow-up command. The ID column now keeps its content width, and the header, like the rows, stays on one line.

  • Fixed --to, --cc and --bcc carrying a display name composing a To: > no SMTP server accepts, as --from did before ([#727]). Each value is now parsed as an address list, so a comma inside a quoted display name ("Doe, Alice" ) no longer splits it.

  • Fixed imap raw hanging until the stream timed out when the last command was not terminated by an explicit \r\n ([#764]).

  • Fixed IMAP searches with non-ASCII text being rejected by Gmail (io-imap#3).

    Bumped io-imap to 0.7.1, whose SEARCH carries CHARSET UTF-8 when its criteria hold non-ASCII text, a fix lost since v1.2.0 (#635). An ASCII search sends no charset, Outlook rejecting the UTF-8 one ([#769]).

  • Fixed the Bcc: field being transmitted over SMTP, disclosing blind recipients to everyone (#747).

    Bumped io-smtp to 0.4, which removes it before DATA. The --save copy and smtp send, whose envelope is explicit, keep it.

  • Fixed a local path carrying a ~ or a shell variable being read verbatim.

    maildir.root = "~/Mail" looked for a directory literally named ~ under the working directory rather than the Maildir the sample documents, and m2dir.root and the tls.cert of every backend read the same way.

    Every path key now expands as the configuration is read, so no reader can forget. pimdir.root and downloads-dir already expanded where they were read, and only moved onto that rule.

  • Fixed a pimdir-only build failing to compile.

    The client-side search evaluation the backend calls was gated on the maildir and m2dir features alone, so --no-default-features --features pimdir did not build. The default feature set was unaffected.

  • Fixed message move and message delete on IMAP servers without the MOVE extension.

    Without MOVE, a move is now UID COPY, \Deleted and, with UIDPLUS, UID EXPUNGE of the copied UIDs. Without UIDPLUS the messages stay flagged \Deleted in the source.

  • Preserved message MIME payloads in gmail threads get --json, including full-format bodies and attachment metadata (#750).

  • Fixed a duplicated message disappearing from the pimdir backend's listing.

    A mailbox holding one Message-ID twice, which a double delivery, a retried append, a restore or a copy of a sent message all produce, used to resolve to a single stored item. One copy was kept and the other recorded on it, mirrored nowhere, so it showed in no listing and could not be read.

    The store now gives the second copy a key of its own, so both list, each with its own public id and neither marked, which is what the mailbox holds. Whether they are duplicates worth removing is the server's state and the user's call, so nothing here merges or hides one.

    Saving a locally-composed message is unchanged: an add naming an id the mailbox already holds parks in the queue instead, the store being liberal with what a sync hands it and strict with what a producer creates.

  • Fixed completion writing files instead of printing the completion script to the standard output ([#736]).

    The script has been documented as going to stdout since the command exists, but the directory it fell back on turned himalaya completion bash into a file-writing command printing a report.

    That broke every packaging helper capturing stdout, Homebrew's generate_completions_from_executable among them. Giving --dir keeps writing one script per shell.

    manual and json-schema follow the same shape, so the three behave alike: they print the single page or schema they are asked for, they take their directory through --dir where it used to be a positional, and they accept command names to select what to generate.

    Restoring the documented behaviour is a regression fix rather than a breaking change, hence the patch release, and generating completions, manual pages or schemas is not a daily gesture.

  • Fixed maildir message copy leaving an empty message behind when the process died mid-copy ([#738]).

    The copy wrote straight to the name the target mailbox lists, so a death inside it left a 0-byte entry envelope list shows as an ordinary message with blank columns, account check calls healthy, and message read alone rejects.

    The copy is now staged and renamed, so an interruption leaves nothing behind.

  • Fixed maildir flag writes doing nothing to a message still unread in a mailbox's new directory ([#637]).

    message read --seen and flag add reported success and left the message untouched, a Maildir name in new having nowhere to carry a flag. The message now moves to cur under the same id with its flags in the name, which is the transition every Maildir client performs.

description:
fix(xlsx): a failed open releases the file before the repair retry

When an .xlsx failed to open (for example a part declaring an XML
encoding the SDK rejects), ExcelHandler's constructor left its
FileStream open. The factory's repair-and-retry then reopened the same
file for an in-place fix and failed with "being used by another
process", so such a file could not be opened for editing at all.

The constructor now disposes the document and its streams on any
failure, like PowerPointHandler does, and still reports a package
error as "Cannot open : ...".

Based on #224 by @Marnie0415 (the ExcelHandler half; the
PowerPointHandler half is already on main).
product_or_resource: fix(xlsx): a failed open releases the file before the repair retry

description:
fix(mcp): a payload read from stdin no longer hangs the MCP server

Under `officecli mcp`, stdin is the JSON-RPC channel and stays open for
the whole session. `batch` without --commands/--input (or with
--input -) and `import --stdin` read stdin to EOF, which never arrives,
and because commands run on the server's request loop every later
request went unanswered until the process was restarted.

Both now refuse immediately under MCP with an error naming the flag
that carries the payload. Outside MCP nothing changes.

Based on #317 by @Lazare-42 (the stdin guard only; the per-command
timeout and output routing are left for a separate change).
product_or_resource: fix(mcp): a payload read from stdin no longer hangs the MCP server

Update Mac launcher and libmozglue for Firefox 153.3.0esr

Build the launcher with the macOS 26.5 SDK. AppKit chooses control metrics
based on the main executable's SDK, so with the old 15.5 launcher, native
buttons and menulists used pre-Tahoe metrics with built-in margins while
Mozilla's XUL (built with 26.5) stopped compensating for them on macOS 26+
(bug 1992898), leaving labels cramped and controls indented.

Also add custom libmozglue.dylib (#6056) and set source info in mozconfig,
which official builds require and which Mozilla only detects automatically
from Mercurial checkouts.

description:
Add `shopify app import channel-config`

Imports the Shopify-authored channel spec for a linked app as a
deployable channel_config extension, so partners migrating off
Shopify-managed specs get a ready-to-edit TOML instead of authoring one
from the docs.

The command calls the App Management endpoint added in shop/world#2051080
(GET /app_management/:version/organizations/:org/apps/:app/channel_spec_export.json)
through a new DeveloperPlatformClient.channelSpecExport method, then
writes specifications/.toml into the app's channel_config
extension:

- reuses the existing channel_config extension if the app has one,
  wherever it lives and whichever TOML layout it uses
- otherwise scaffolds extensions/channel-config, but aborts before
  writing if extension_directories wouldn't discover it or another
  extension already occupies that directory
- --force to overwrite an existing spec; --json for machine output

Status handling mirrors the server contract: 200 success, 422 with a
reason code for well-formed "not exportable" failures, 404 as
endpoint/app unavailable, 426 as outdated CLI, 401/403 as auth.

The command is hidden while the backend is allowlist-gated to a small
cohort of channel partners.

description:
feat: date-range filtering (since/until) for search_messages

Adds optional since (inclusive) and until (exclusive) ISO datetime bounds to
search_messages across store, client, MCP tool schema/dispatch and the
'search' CLI command (--since/--until). Applied in both the FTS and LIKE
fallback paths. Lets the AI answer 'what did X say about Y last week'
in one call instead of paging through all-time results.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5

perf: batch desktop-import commits and cap webhook POST concurrency

Signal Desktop import previously committed once per message (thousands
of commits for a large history); now batches in chunks of 500 via the
new store.save_messages_batch. webhook.post_webhook_batch previously
fired every outbound POST concurrently with no limit; capped to 10
in-flight requests so a large catch-up batch can't open hundreds of
simultaneous connections.

Part of a security + performance audit of signal-mcp; these were the
two confirmed, fixable performance issues. No security fixes were
needed — reviewed daemon binding, SQL parameterization, file
permissions, desktop-import key handling, attachment path traversal,
command construction, and error/log surfaces; all were sound.
